articles.title: How AI Helps Recyclers Turn Mixed Waste Into Reusable Material
articles.summary:
As world leaders gather for COP31 in Türkiye, the event’s emphasis on zero waste puts a practical challenge in focus: how to keep products and materials in use for longer. Globally, less than 7% of the materials entering the economy come from recycled or reused sources. Municipal solid waste generation accounts for over 2 billion tons of trash per year — a figure that could nearly double by 2050.
AI and robotics are helping change this trajectory, as innovators around the globe improve sorting to recover resources that would otherwise end up in landfills.
“A more circular economy relies on making better use of what we already have,” said Josh Parker, head of sustainability at NVIDIA. “AI can help us understand what’s in a waste stream, identify what can be recovered and automate the work of sorting it. We’re giving innovators the computing tools to make those processes more effective and bring them to more places.”
See how four members of the NVIDIA Inception program for startups are applying AI to keep valuable materials in circulation.
Recycled plastic is only used if its cost and quality can compete with new material. Too often it can’t: Incoming waste is of inconsistent quality, sorting depends on hard-to-find manual labor and mixed scrap ends up downcycled into low-grade products.

articles.title: Más de 35.000 aplicaciones creadas con Grok quedaron abiertas a cualquiera, con datos médicos y de empleados
articles.summary:
Una firma de seguridad informática encontró que más de 35.000 aplicaciones creadas con Grok, el asistente de inteligencia artificial de Elon Musk, podían abrirse sin iniciar sesión. Entre ellas había documentos confidenciales de la propia empresa, resultados médicos de pacientes y listas de empleados de compañías grandes.
La firma, Claroc, publicó el hallazgo el 10 de noviembre. Probó 43.551 direcciones de aplicaciones publicadas con Grok: 37.571 seguían en línea y 35.578 (94,7%) se abrían para cualquiera, sin pedir identificación. Solo 1.993 respondían con un error de acceso denegado.
Claroc calculó que una de cada 10 aplicaciones abiertas contenía material sensible, datos internos de empresas o información personal, y que cerca del 2% guardaba material de gravedad alta o crítica. La mayoría eran juegos, páginas de presentación y calculadoras.
Grok permite describir una aplicación en el chat para que el asistente la programe y luego publicarla en una dirección propia, que termina en grok.me. Según Claroc, al publicar una aplicación en su cuenta de prueba, la opción preseleccionada era “cualquiera con el enlace”.

articles.title: Imagem histórica de buraco negro resiste a novo teste científico
articles.summary:
Uma análise independente dos dados usados para produzir a primeira imagem de um buraco negro, divulgada em 2019, confirmou a estrutura brilhante em forma de anel ao redor de uma região escura. Os resultados foram publicados em 11 de novembro na revista científica Nature.
O estudo corrobora amplamente as descobertas originais do Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), mas mantém em aberto questões sobre a distribuição do brilho e os métodos utilizados para reconstruir a imagem.
Reanálise reforça resultado de 2019
A colaboração internacional EHT apresentou, em 2019, a primeira imagem da sombra de um buraco negro. O registro mostrava um anel brilhante ao redor de uma região central escura, estrutura compatível com as previsões da teoria da relatividade geral de Albert Einstein.
Para produzir a imagem, o projeto combina observações simultâneas de radiotelescópios instalados em diferentes continentes. Juntos, os equipamentos funcionam como um único telescópio virtual, com resolução equivalente à de uma antena com dimensões próximas às da Terra.
A reconstrução, porém, enfrenta limitações. Como os radiotelescópios não cobrem toda a superfície terrestre, existem lacunas nas observações, que precisam ser compensadas por métodos matemáticos e modelos computacionais. As escolhas feitas nesse processo podem influenciar o resultado final.

La Mini 2 règle le problème. Selon la fiche technique publiée par Starlink, la batterie fait 71 Wh pour 490 grammes et se clipse à l’arrière de l’antenne. Months earlier, he’d singled out a way to get viewers to spend more time with Paramount’s programming. A feed of short vertical videos, he said, was “critical to our future.”
Streaming is still trying to be TikTok
It hasn’t proven that short-form video will help.

articles.title: Estados Unidos batirá en 2026 su tercer récord seguido de consumo de electricidad, con la IA como motor
articles.summary:
El consumo de electricidad en Estados Unidos llegará a un récord de 4.306 mil millones de kilovatios hora en 2026 y a unos 4.370 mil millones en 2027, según la Administración de Información de Energía (EIA), el organismo estadístico del Departamento de Energía.
En 2025 el consumo fue de 4.216 mil millones, también un máximo histórico. Si la proyección se cumple, 2026 será el tercer año consecutivo de récord, según Reuters sobre el informe que la EIA publicó el 10 de noviembre.
La agencia atribuye el aumento sobre todo a los centros de datos dedicados a la inteligencia artificial y a que hogares y empresas usan más electricidad y menos combustibles fósiles para calefacción y transporte.
El texto de la EIA explica el alza de otro modo: señala como causas la demanda del sector comercial, que agrupa comercios, oficinas y otros servicios, y las altas temperaturas del último verano.
El sector comercial pasará a los hogares
Las ventas de electricidad al sector comercial llegarán en 2026 a 1.557 mil millones de kilovatios hora, según las tablas de la EIA. Los hogares consumirán 1.546 mil millones, de modo que el sector comercial quedará por encima del residencial.
Ambos superan sus marcas de 2025: 1.503 mil millones para el comercio y 1.519 mil millones para las viviendas. La industria, con 1.061 mil millones, quedará apenas debajo de su máximo de 2000, de 1.064 mil millones.

articles.title: Choosing QuePaxa, an unusual consensus algorithm
articles.summary:
Choosing QuePaxa, an unusual consensus algorithm
Cloudflare recently announced Meerkat, an experimental distributed consensus service designed to manage our internal global control plane. It is powered by a new consensus algorithm published by researchers Tennage & Băsescu et al. called QuePaxa (2023).
QuePaxa is an unusual choice; most consensus systems use well-established consensus algorithms like Raft, (Multi-)Paxos or Viewstamped Replication. These algorithms are well understood, have mature implementations, and usually work well.
Unfortunately, common consensus algorithms often suffer in wide-area networks with volatile network connectivity and latency, i.e., networks like the Internet, which is where Meerkat runs. These algorithms rely on a single leader process being available and having predictable latency. If the leader goes down, experiences higher latency than usual, or is disconnected, the entire consensus system slows down or becomes unavailable until the leader is replaced. This is unacceptable for Meerkat.
Meerkat’s global deployment environment led us to a newer consensus algorithm, QuePaxa, which promises better stability despite volatility, in large part by not relying on a leader to make progress. In this post we’ll explain why we chose QuePaxa and how the QuePaxa algorithm works.

articles.title: „Wir haben es schon einmal geschafft”: Was Österreichs Protestkultur über Tech-Widerstand lehrt
articles.summary:
Bürgerprotest: Was ein nie gestartetes AKW über Googles Rechenzentrum lehrt
„Another Zwentendorf is possible“ steht in großen schwarzen Lettern auf dem Transparent vor mir. Ich bin in Linz, der drittgrößten Stadt Österreichs, und besuche das Ars-Electronica-Festival. Rund 30 Kilometer außerhalb, in Kronstorf, entsteht das größte Rechenzentrum des Landes. Ein Hyperscaler, der einmal so viel Strom verbrauchen soll wie die Hauptstadt Wien.
Der Standort ist das Gegenteil einer Millionenmetropole. Das beschauliche Kronstorf zählt gerade einmal 3500 Seelen. Vor 18 Jahren hat der Tech-Konzern Google dort ein Stück Land erworben und mit den Jahren wurde das Vorhaben immer größer. Was einst als Cloud-Infrastruktur und wirtschaftliche Chance angepriesen wurde, steht heute vor allem für zwei Buchstaben: KI. Das Rechenzentrum soll die enormen Rechenkapazitäten dafür bereitstellen.
Die ökologischen Kosten trägt die Region. Nicht einmal eine Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfung ist vorgesehen. Und das, obwohl das Rechenzentrum erwärmtes, mit Chemikalien versetztes Wasser in die Enns leiten wird. Die Genehmigungen sind erteilt, die Bagger rollen. Die Geschichte aus Kronstorf scheint auserzählt und wird – so scheint es – mit der Inbetriebnahme des Rechenzentrums enden. Doch seit dem Sommer regt sich Widerstand. In the annals of industrial history, few innovations have demonstrated such remarkable staying power as the dynamo-electric principle. Discovered by Werner von Siemens in 1866, this groundbreaking principle remains fundamental to modern electrical engineering more than a century and a half later – and continues to shape the technology portfolio of Innomotics, a globally leading provider of electric motors and large drive systems. What began as a breakthrough in electromechanical energy conversion has evolved into a cornerstone of global industry – powering everything from brewery operations in Qingdao to high-voltage drive systems in petrochemical plants.
1866: The breakthrough that powered the future
The year 1866 marked a decisive turning point, not only in the broader arc of industrial transformation but specifically in the realm of electric motion. At a time when Europe was entering a new phase of industrial transformation, Werner von Siemens pioneered the dynamo-electric principle – a breakthrough that enabled electric machines to generate their own magnetic field through self-excitation. This innovation transformed electric machines from laboratory curiosities into practical power sources, enabling the widespread electrification of industry and infrastructure that defined the late 19th century.

articles.summary:

La compañía no informó que las fallas se hayan explotado en ataques reales. El sitio MacRumors advirtió que, con los detalles ya públicos, los equipos sin actualizar quedan más expuestos. La versión llega dos semanas después de iOS 27.2 y no trae funciones nuevas.

Dos fallas en los chats grupales de iMessage
La primera falla, según Apple, era un problema de autorización: un atacante remoto podía sumarse a un grupo de iMessage sin ser invitado y recibir los mensajes del chat. La empresa la corrigió con una validación más estricta. Un investigador anónimo la reportó.
La segunda afectaba a alguien que ya había sido añadido al grupo: podía ver los mensajes enviados antes de su ingreso. Apple la resolvió eliminando el código vulnerable. También la descubrió un investigador anónimo.
Las notas de Apple no indican que alguna conversación haya sido leída ni cuántos usuarios resultaron afectados. Describen lo que un atacante podría haber hecho, no lo que ocurrió.

articles.title: Threat Actors Exploit Openwave, Cisco BroadWorks Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Threat actors are exploiting two vulnerabilities in Openwave Webtop Media Transcoder and Cisco BroadWorks to access sensitive information.
Openwave Messaging provides email and messaging platforms, including webmail, to communication service providers. Webtop Media Transcoder handles document conversion, and Openwave’s advisory ties it to the company’s webmail.
The Webtop Media Transcoder bug, tracked as CVE-2026-111793, exists because administrator-defined file-type restrictions are not enforced, allowing users to convert unintended file types.
“This may allow an authenticated user to process and convert unintended document types if bypassing the webmail experience,” Openwave Messaging explains in an advisory.
Webtop Media Transcoder version 1.1.22.0, which rolled out in December 2021, contains patches. The security defect was disclosed on October 7, and a CVE record was published on October 16.
Japan JVN flagged the weakness as exploited on November 9, warning that an authenticated attacker could exploit it to upload a specially crafted file and obtain sensitive information.
The Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-20320, was disclosed on August 19 as an out-of-band blind XML external entity injection that could be exploited remotely, without authentication, to read sensitive configuration information.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. articles.title: Rusia tenía un campo vacío junto a Ucrania. Seis semanas después, los satélites han revelado una fábrica de pesadillas letales
articles.summary:
Lo hemos ido contando. La guerra de Ucrania también se está librando a través de las imágenes que captan los satélites comerciales. Las últimas han revelado una transformación extraordinaria junto a la frontera rusa, y lo más inquietante no es únicamente lo que ha aparecido allí, sino la velocidad a la que Moscú ha conseguido levantarlo.
De campo vacío a instalación militar en semanas. El 8 de agosto de 2026, las imágenes de satélite de Vantor y Planet Labs mostraban un terreno prácticamente vacío cerca de Millerovo, en el suroeste de Rusia, a unos tres kilómetros de una base aérea. El pasado 12 de septiembre ya aparecían caminos de acceso, explanaciones y espacios preparados para nuevas estructuras. Nueve días después se distinguían terraplenes, posiciones de lanzamiento y cimientos, mientras que el 12 de octubre ya eran visibles edificios de almacenamiento e instalaciones de apoyo.
En apenas seis semanas, Rusia había transformado un campo en una base militar avanzada. Para Spencer Faragasso, investigador del Institute for Science and International Security, la velocidad de construcción demuestra que Moscú está perfeccionando una capacidad tan importante como fabricar armas: levantar rápidamente la infraestructura necesaria para utilizarlas.

articles.title: Crean un robot blando que se mueve con microalgas y luz: cómo funciona
articles.summary:
Durante décadas, la robótica blanda buscó respuesta a una pregunta aparentemente simple: ¿cómo hacer que una máquina se mueva sin motores, cables ni baterías? Los actuadores convencionales, los mecanismos que convierten energía en movimiento, dependen de sistemas eléctricos o mecánicos que limitan su autonomía y su compatibilidad con entornos delicados como el agua o los tejidos vivos.
La búsqueda de alternativas biológicas llevó a explorar células cardíacas, levaduras y bacterias, pero ninguna lograba combinar reversibilidad, durabilidad y una fuente de energía verdaderamente autónoma.
Algo tan pequeño e inesperado como las microalgas resultó ser la respuesta. Investigadores de la Universidad Tecnológica de Delft (TU Delft), en los Países Bajos, desarrollaron un brazo robótico blando impulsado únicamente por la luz, sin ninguna fuente de energía externa.
El dispositivo, de apenas 2 centímetros de largo y 1 milímetro de grosor, está recubierto de microalgas vivas cuya actividad fotosintética genera los movimientos de flexión necesarios para agarrar y levantar objetos. Los resultados fueron publicados en la revista Nature Communications.
El hallazgo central es que las microalgas son el motor. Su metabolismo, que varía según la presencia o ausencia de luz, altera el nivel de acidez del hidrogel, lo que provoca que el actuador se doble en una dirección u otra. Chez Anthropic, un reset remet à zéro les compteurs déjà consommés, sans relever les plafonds eux-mêmes. Pour rappel, Claude fonctionne avec deux jauges : une limite par session de cinq heures et une limite hebdomadaire, qui se recharge à un jour et une heure fixes, propres à chaque compte.
Celui-ci est le plus généreux qu’Anthropic ait distribué : il remplit à nouveau la session en cours et la limite hebdomadaire, tous modèles confondus. Les « resets Fable » offerts le 9 novembre pour le lancement de Claude Fable 5.2 étaient plus ciblés : ils ne rendaient que la consommation hebdomadaire passée sur les modèles Fable, en plus de recharger la session de cinq heures. Synopsys’ Charlie Matar finds that interconnects are becoming more influential components of both the silicon and system architecture, with AI infrastructure compute scaling only if data reaches the right processor at the right time at an acceptable power cost.

Arm’s Emanuele Rocca highlights security features designed to mitigate Control Flow attacks, in which successful exploits overwrite the return address of the function currently executing or the target pointer of an upcoming jump with the address of a memory area controlled by the attacker.

articles.title: Validating GPU Platforms with Runtime AI Inventory via the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
As teams deploy and scale AI workloads using NVIDIA Dynamo, Kubeflow, or Slurm, tracking what actually runs requires visibility beyond the platform configuration captured in a recipe. Application teams define and update these workloads independently of the platform recipe, so a reproducible deployment bundle alone cannot establish which workload artifacts are running on each node. Mutable image tags like :latest add another layer of complexity. Two nodes can end up running different code under identical tags, and a node that pulls next week may retrieve an image that was not covered by an earlier security review.
NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR), an open source modular component of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, now includes a qualified AI bill of materials (AIBOM) component to close that gap. An open source project created by Google, k8s-aibom tracks AI workloads running on Kubernetes. Two stock recipes select k8s-aibom by default: h100-gke-cos-inference and h100-gke-cos-inference-dynamo. Other GKE recipes can opt in during generation with --runtime-inventory enabled. Recipes selecting it can opt out with --runtime-inventory disabled.
AICR turns known-good GPU platform configurations into version-locked recipes and reproducible deployment bundles. Each recipe records the desired configuration for one hardware, cloud, OS, and intent combination: its components, version pins, values, constraints, deployment ordering, and validation expectations. AICR generates reproducibl…

articles.title: MP da Espanha abre investigação contra TikTok por conteúdo ilegal

O Ministério Público da Espanha determinou nesta quarta-feira (11) a abertura de uma investigação sobre a suposta divulgação de material de abuso sexual infantil no TikTok. A medida atende a uma denúncia da fundação espanhola Maldita.es, que identificou mais de mil vídeos desse tipo na plataforma.
Segundo a organização, os conteúdos acumulavam 48 milhões de visualizações, mas o TikTok teria removido apenas 10% do material denunciado.
A Maldita.es, que já havia investigado o problema em outras duas ocasiões, também apontou que a rede social bloqueou somente 26% do conteúdo ilegal identificado na Espanha. A organização identificou ainda mais de 26 mil perfis de possíveis pedófilos que trocavam ou vendiam material de abuso sexual infantil na plataforma. Desse total, aproximadamente 7.700 utilizavam o idioma espanhol.
Investigação encontrou transmissões ao vivo com crianças
A apuração também identificou quase uma centena de transmissões ao vivo em 17 países nas quais espectadores pediam que crianças realizassem determinadas ações em troca de dinheiro. Algumas das solicitações tinham natureza sexual.
Embora as regras do TikTok proíbam menores de idade de realizar lives, a organização encontrou esse tipo de transmissão na plataforma. A fundação também apontou falhas no mecanismo de busca da rede social, que não bloqueava palavras-chave relacionadas a esses conteúdos, diferentemente do que ocorre em outras plataformas.

articles.title: Dreeze Emerges From Stealth With $33M to Rebuild Cloud Apps After Cyberattacks
articles.summary:
Cloud application recovery startup Dreeze announced on Tuesday that it raised $33 million in a seed funding round as it emerged from stealth mode with a platform built to bring back whole cloud applications instead of only the data behind them.
The round was led by Norwest and Bessemer Venture Partners, with Claltech also investing.
Dreeze, whose staff is split between Israel and the United States, said the money will go toward product development, bigger sales and marketing teams, and getting its platform into more enterprises.
The company was formed in 2025 by Avi Raichel and brothers Ziv and Oded Kedem. The three previously worked together at Zerto, which HPE acquired, and Kashya.
Dreeze’s argument is that getting data back after an incident is not the same as getting an application running again. A cyberattack or a mistake by an AI agent can leave an organization with its data intact but without the configurations, secrets, infrastructure and connections the application needs.
Its platform, named Application Revival, scans the customer’s cloud environment on an ongoing basis, works out which resources and dependencies belong to which application, and generates a recovery plan from the live environment. Backups of data and configurations are stored with those recovery plans in an immutable, isolated vault under the customer’s control.

articles.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
articles.summary:
Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in our DNA affect different cells, giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease — and point the way to new treatments.
Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
DeepMind’s new DNA model better predicts how mutations affect different cells, potentially opening paths to treatment.
AlphaGenome 2 is the successor to DeepMind’s genome-predicting AI model AlphaGenome, which was released last year. While nearly every cell in the human body carries the same DNA, different types of cells — from heart muscle cells and skin cells to immune cells fighting an infection — switch different genes on and off, and those patterns can change depending on what a cell is doing. As a result, the same genetic variant can have very different effects depending on the type and state of the cell.
The new model is designed to capture those differences, predicting the effects of genetic variants on individual cell types and states. Google said in a blog post published Wednesday that it offers a much finer-grained view than broader models like AlphaGenome, potentially revealing disease-relevant effects in specific cells that might otherwise go unnoticed.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

articles.title: The Evolution of Commercial Open Source Software
articles.summary:
The Evolution of Commercial Open Source Software
Tony Wasserman | 11 November 2026
The Early Days
In the early days of computing, there were no software products. Some computer systems vendors provided mechanisms for their customers to freely distribute applications with their source code, typically through their user groups (e.g, IBM SHARE Library) [1]. Applications were custom-built, developed across many different computer systems using a wide variety of different languages.
The 1964 arrival and subsequent broad adoption of IBM’s System/360 and OS/360 made it feasible for developers to build software products that could be licensed to a large number of buyers. Soon thereafter, Martin Goetz was able to patent a software algorithm and to release Autoflow, the first commercial software product. Those steps led to today’s multi-billion dollar commercial software industry, with vendor-licensed products, accompanied by End User Software Agreements and patents.
Shareware
While vendors focused on enterprises and governments, the arrival of personal computers in the mid-1970s, created a consumer market for software products. In addition to vendor supported products such as Microsoft BASIC, other programs, collectively known as “shareware”, were developed by individuals, with their users asked to make a small donation (under $50 US) to the developer. Some of the most popular applications of this category were PC-Talk, PC-File, PC-Write, and WinRAR, all of which attracted many thousa…

UCIe provides a common standard for die-to-die connectivity, but connecting dies in a 2.5D package is fundamentally different from connecting them in a 3D design.
In 2.5D designs, UCIe links traverse package channels where insertion loss, crosstalk, and increasing data rates influence PHY and package design. In 3D designs, shorter vertical connections and fine-pitch bonding allow bandwidth to scale through connection density, reducing the need for high-speed serialization, equalization, and channel training.
This white paper examines those differences and the engineering considerations behind choosing and implementing UCIe connectivity for advanced multi-die designs.

articles.title: Angular's TypeScript 7-Powered Compiler Enters Beta with Rust-Based Preprocessor
articles.summary:
The Angular team has shared details of a new version of its compiler, the Angular Preprocessor (ngp), which rewrites the analysis stage of the toolchain in Rust to clear the way for TypeScript 7 adoption. Alex Rickabaugh and Mark Techson announced the work on the Angular team blog in late September, shortly after Microsoft shipped TypeScript 7.0, whose Go-based rewrite removed the ts.Transformer API that Angular's ahead-of-time compiler depends on.
The existing compiler, ngc, wraps tsc and uses the Transformer API to turn decorators such as @Component and @Pipe into runtime instructions. The Go port offers no cross-language equivalent, and crossing the JS/Go boundary at every file would be prohibitive. The Angular team's answer is to decouple compilation from TypeScript's APIs and rebuild it on Oxc, the VoidZero Rust toolchain already powering Vite. The team pointed to the plan on X, framing it as a partial rewrite rather than a fresh start.
ngp runs in three stages. A Rust frontend using Oxc analyses files in parallel to discover Angular declarations and resolve metadata. The existing TypeScript template compiler then emits two artefacts, a runtime file containing the transformed component and a .ngtypecheck.ts file holding the Type Check Block (TCB) for template type-checking. Finally a downstream tool, whether tsgo, tsrs, esbuild or Rolldown, handles type-checking and JavaScript emission independently.

Los buitres se enfrentan a diario a un festín que para cualquier otro animal podría ser una causa de muerte casi inmediata. Y es que, al alimentarse de cadáveres que están en descomposición, también se están comiendo un cóctel masivo de microorganismos y bacterias que son potencialmente mortales.
Lo que se pensaba. La intuición sugería que esta dieta tan extrema terminaría por igualar la flora bacteriana de las distintas especies carroñeras, dotándolas de un microbioma que estuviera especializado en poder procesar la carne podrida. Sin embargo, un nuevo estudio acaba de desmontar esta idea, puesto que la genética y la especie de cada individuo actúan como un filtro anatómico mucho más estricto que el menú que comparten.
El estudio. Ha sido publicado en PNAS y ha estado liderado por el propio CSIC, y recoge cómo los investigadores analizaron muestras de 155 aves silvestres en el Pirineo, la gran mayoría en territorio de Aragón. Aquí el trabajo incluyó ejemplares de las cuatro especies de buitres europeos, es decir, el quebrantahuesos, el buitre leonado, el alimoche y el buitre negro, además del milano real, una rapaz que ejerce como carroñera, pero no de forma exclusiva.
Aquí, el investigador Michael Wink lo explica perfectamente: “Uno de los hallazgos más interesantes es que no existe un único microbioma característico de los buitres. articles.title: À la recherche de la preuve parfaite : Google a lâché 80 agents IA sur le code de Signal pour prouver qu’il était sûr

Pendant quatre semaines, des équipes comptant jusqu’à 80 agents d’IA ont travaillé sans interruption sur les machines de cinq chercheurs de Google DeepMind, avec une mission précise, démontrer mathématiquement que le code qui chiffre les conversations Signal tient ses promesses de sécurité.
Google a dévoilé le résultat le 10 novembre 2026. Le travail porte sur libsignal, la bibliothèque qui met en œuvre le protocole de chiffrement de bout en bout de Signal, dont des variantes équipent aussi WhatsApp, Messenger et Google Messages.
Prouver plutôt que tester
D’ordinaire, on évalue la sécurité d’un logiciel en le testant, en l’auditant ou en y cherchant des failles, ce qui permet d’affirmer qu’aucun problème n’a été trouvé, sans garantir qu’il n’en existe aucun.
Mais il existe une autre approche, la vérification formelle.
Reposant sur des méthodes mathématiques, elle consiste à démontrer, comme on le ferait pour un théorème, que le code ne peut pas enfreindre certaines propriétés. Problème, la méthode est réputée extrêmement coûteuse. La vérification de seL4, un noyau de système d’exploitation dont des chercheurs australiens ont démontré formellement le bon fonctionnement en 2009, a par exemple demandé l’équivalent de vingt ans de travail pour une seule personne.
Et c’est à cela que s’est attaqué Google DeepMind avec AlphaProof Code.

articles.title: 3 protections déjà incluses dans votre VPN, et que presque personne n’active

Vous utilisez peut-être un VPN pour masquer votre adresse IP ou protéger votre connexion. Pourtant, si vous avez souscrit à CyberGhost, il est probable que vous disposiez d’outils supplémentaires très utiles afin de sécuriser davantage votre navigation et vos données personnelles. Voici comment les activer.
Installer l’application de votre VPN sur un smartphone ou un ordinateur et cliquer sur le bouton de connexion suffit pour chiffrer votre trafic Internet par le biais d’un serveur privé virtuel.
Certaines offres limitées s’arrêtent là, mais ce n’est pas le cas de CyberGhost : en plus d’une connexion VPN, ce service donne accès à plusieurs outils et fonctionnalités utiles, mais pas toujours connus des utilisateurs. Quelques minutes suffisent pour les configurer.
CyberGhost VPN en fait plus que vous ne le pensez

Low Power-High Performance
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
How a flexible binary can serve every length up to the capacity you set.
								November 11th, 2026 - 
								By: Quadric.io
								
							
If you are sizing a language model for an edge product, the prompts it will see span a wide range. A spoken command is a dozen tokens, a pasted document is several thousand, and the same device serves both. Somewhere in the software stack, a decision is made about the gap between the longest prompt you provisioned for and the prompt that actually arrives. That decision sets how many binaries you build and qualify. It also sets how much of every inference is spent computing padding.
Most compiled inference stacks do not make that decision at all. A graph compiled for 1024 tokens processes 1024 positions every time it runs. If you send it 50 tokens, it computes the other 974 as padding. To serve short prompts efficiently as well as long ones, you have to build a separate binary for each length range and qualify all of them. Quadric Chimera GPNPU does not work this way. It gives you one guarantee and one optimization.

articles.title: The iOS Crash We Could Not Reproduce
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Intermittent production crashes often need controlled fault isolation when logs and local testing cannot identify the failing path.
- A lower overall crash rate does not prove that the root cause is fixed. Unrelated changes can simply change the timing of a concurrency defect.
- One device that reproduces a failure probabilistically can turn speculative debugging into testable engineering work.
- HTML import through NSAttributedString has a main-thread requirement that is easy to miss when the call sits inside asynchronous screen preparation.
- A shared main-actor abstraction is a stronger safeguard than asking every call site to remember a framework threading rule.
Some production crashes announce themselves with a clean stack trace. This one did not. It appeared in a large-scale consumer iOS application, affected only some executions, and resisted every local reproduction attempt. The final code change was small, but reaching it required turning a vague SIGBUS report into a controlled set of experiments. This article walks through the investigation and the threading contract behind HTML import in NSAttributedString.
The Crash That Refused to Reproduce
Most production crashes I investigate start with a familiar routine. I read the crash report, look for the stack frame closest to the failure, try to reproduce the path, and then work backward toward the root cause. This incident did not fit that pattern.

La empresa lo describió en una publicación en su sitio y afirmó que ya funciona en su infraestructura de investigación.
El mecanismo opera sobre cada tarea de investigación que usa un modelo: entrenamientos, evaluaciones y procesamiento de datos, incluidas las tareas en las que el modelo actúa por pasos y por su cuenta. Cada tarea recibe un número de identificación al empezar. Antes de generar cada respuesta, el motor que ejecuta el modelo consulta a Control Room si esa tarea sigue autorizada.

El programa de la tarea puede seguir encendido, pero ya no recibe nada del modelo. OpenAI sostiene que no depende de que ese programa obedezca la orden de parada.
La empresa exige que toda tarea de este tipo tenga un caso de seguridad aprobado. Además, los entrenamientos más avanzados corren con un monitor: otro modelo que revisa todo lo que hace el modelo en entrenamiento y levanta una alerta si detecta un problema. Oli Lane: A few years back, I have this really vivid memory of a customer complaint coming in. It was late on a Friday, of course, they always are. They said, my backup job ran like an hour late, what's going on? They were pretty annoyed, rightly so, they need to trust that our backup product works, and it's solid and it's dependable. Of course, we dug in. We had our dashboards. We had our metrics. We had our logs. We had our alerts. We did some rooting around, we came up with some plausible theories. There was this thing that didn't sit right with me and it was that we never really figured out the most important question, which was, why did that job run late and why was it late that time? This talk is the story of getting from there, where we're squinting at graphs and making a good guess, but mostly shrugging to being able to point and explain the exact bottleneck in a distributed asynchronous system.

articles.title: Developers have been hacking around MCP’s file-upload problem for two years. A fix is taking shape.
articles.summary:
Developers have been hacking around MCP’s file-upload problem for two years. A fix is taking shape.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has played an instrumental part in connecting AI assistants to external tools and data since Anthropic launched the project some two years ago. Want to have a coding agent check the status of a bug? Give it access to your issue tracker through an MCP server. Or ask an assistant how many orders your company shipped last week? Connect it to a tool that can query your database.
Part of the Agentic AI Foundation since last December, MCP has a roadmap that reflects the demands of running the protocol in production. For instance, maintainers have been working to make servers easier to deploy without keeping track of individual client sessions, and to let companies manage access through their existing identity systems.
But a perennial problem developers have faced is how to pass a file from an AI app to an MCP tool. For example, say you attach a PDF to a chat and ask the assistant to save it to cloud storage — the assistant can call a tool to save the file, but developers still have to work out how to get the PDF from the chat app to the tool. That can mean issuing a temporary upload link, or perhaps sending the user to a separate upload page.
To address this gap, the folks at the MCP project have outlined a draft extension that gives clients and tools a common way to handle uploads and downloads.

QCon AI New York 2026 has published its full schedule for December 15–16. Engineers from LinkedIn, Netflix, DoorDash, Figma, and other organizations will examine the architecture and operational decisions behind production AI systems, including agent authorization, evaluation pipelines, model serving, and AI-assisted software delivery. With the conference a few weeks away, there is still time to join other practitioners before the full ticket price takes effect on December 9.
The program addresses questions facing teams moving beyond initial AI deployments: where to enforce agent permissions, how to connect offline evaluations to production behavior, and how to support growing inference workloads. It also examines how coding agents affect code review, engineering practices, and organizational adoption.
The following presentations explore these challenges through systems the speakers build and operate.
Keynotes
Nancy Wang, CTO at 1Password, who founded and scaled AWS Data Protection and previously worked at Rubrik and Google, opens day one with When Software Becomes a User: Identity and Authorization for Agents in Production. She argues that identity systems assume a human behind every credential, with a stable role, a bounded session, and someone accountable afterward. Agents have none of these.

articles.title: El remake de "Zelda: Ocarina of Time" vendió 5,2 millones de copias en cuatro días
articles.summary:
Nintendo vendió más de 5,2 millones de copias de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time para la consola Switch 2 en los primeros cuatro días tras su lanzamiento, el 5 de noviembre. Es la mayor cifra de ventas en un estreno de un juego publicado por la marca para esa consola, según informó la compañía.
De ese total, 810.000 unidades se vendieron en Japón, precisó la empresa en su comunicado. El juego es una recreación completa del título original de 1998 para la consola Nintendo 64, con gráficos renovados y mejoras de jugabilidad que preservan la experiencia original, indica la compañía.
El juego salió a la venta en todo el mundo a USD 59.99. Bloomberg informó que acumula 96 puntos sobre 100 en Metacritic, un sitio que reúne las notas de la prensa y de los jugadores, tanto en la valoración de los críticos como en la de los usuarios.
Solo Mario Kart World vendió más unidades en la Switch 2, según Bloomberg, que recordó que ese título formó parte del paquete de lanzamiento de la consola. El remake de Zelda ya superó las ventas acumuladas de Donkey Kong Bananza, otro título popular de 2025.
Una consola que esperaba un éxito
Bloomberg describió el primer año de la Switch 2 como irregular, con precios de equipos más altos por el encarecimiento de la memoria. El medio comparó el efecto potencial con el de la primera Switch, que en 2017 salió con The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild y atrajo a jugadores ajenos a Nintendo.

articles.title: Inside the economics of OPay and Moniepoint’s business
articles.summary:
A Bolt driver in Nigeria will likely ask you to pay via OPay at the end of a trip, while a local store is more likely to have a Moniepoint terminal at its checkout. Both fintechs, which hold microfinance banking licences, have become synonymous with scale in Nigeria’s payments market, carving out niches in consumer payments and merchant processing.
In 2025, Nigeria processed more than ₦1.2 quadrillion ($880.51 billion) worth of electronic transactions. Moniepoint and OPay accounted for a significant share of this activity, processing a combined $644.85 billion.
Moniepoint said it processed 14 billion transactions worth ₦412 trillion ($286.85 billion at ₦1,436.31/$ as of December 31, 2025) in 2025. OPay processed 62.3 billion transactions worth $358 billion. OPay processed 4.45 times as many transactions as Moniepoint, but Moniepoint’s average transaction value was $20.49, approximately 3.56 times OPay’s $5.75.
Moniepoint said it serves more than 20 million businesses and individuals, while OPay reported 50.1 million monthly active users.
These numbers offer a window into the operating economics of both companies: who moves more money, who makes more money from moving it, and who keeps more of what they make?
It is important to note that Moniepoint operates largely in Nigeria, with a recent expansion into Kenya. OPay operates in Indonesia, Egypt, and Pakistan, but derives most of its scale from Nigeria. It generated 88.1% of its revenue from the country in 2025.

articles.title: Les radars militaires peuvent désactiver une partie de votre réseau Wi-Fi et vous ne pouvez rien faire
articles.summary:
Vous êtes chez vous, et le canal 5 GHz de votre réseau Wi-Fi se coupe d’un seul coup : tous vos appareils basculent alors sur le 2,4 GHz, parfois avec peine. Aucune explication, vous vous dites que c’est un bug ; peut-être que vous redémarrez votre box. En réalité, c’est peut-être à cause d’un radar militaire si ce canal s’est coupé.
Le canal 5 GHz de votre réseau Wi-Fi se coupe tout seul ? C’est peut-être normal
Effectivement, votre box Internet ou votre routeur Wi-Fi peut parfois abandonner brutalement le canal 5 GHz et tout faire basculer sur le 2,4 GHz. Si vous avez un écran dessus, ou un journal, il y aura peut-être un message affiché, indiquant simplement « radar ». Il ne s’agit généralement pas d’un bug, mais d’un mécanisme réglementaire, baptisé Dynamic Frequency Selection (DFS).
Il oblige le Wi-Fi à céder la place aux radars, y compris les radars militaires. En France, les bandes 5 GHz ne sont pas entièrement libres : une partie est partagée avec des services prioritaires, notamment des radars. C’est l’ANFR, l’Agence Nationale des Fréquences Radio, qui gère les bandes de fréquences dans le pays. Concernant les bandes 5 GHz, parmi les radars prioritaires il y a ceux dédiés à la météorologie, l’aéronautique, l’armée, ou pour les communications satellites. Donc lorsqu’un routeur Wi-Fi détecte un signal radar sur le canal qu’il utilise, il doit arrêter d’émettre sur ce canal et en choisir un autre, le plus souvent le 2,4 GHz, qu’on trouve sur tous les routeurs.

Microsoft has fixed Outlook sign-in and mail delivery issues on Exchange Server systems after installing the October 2026 Windows Server security updates.
Microsoft acknowledged this known issue in mid-October, confirming that users had trouble accessing email or signing in to Outlook after installing the latest updates on systems running Windows Server 2019 and later.
As explained at the time, the sign-in and mail flow issues are caused by a new default limit on the amount of memory Endpoint Mapper uses when handling Endpoint Lookup calls, introduced by the October 2026 updates.
"After installing the October 2026 Windows security update [..], some on-premises Exchange servers might experience issues accessing or sending email. Users might be unable to sign in to Outlook on the web (OWA), or email messages sent from Outlook might remain in the Outbox and not be delivered. Additionally, Exchange might experience issues accessing mailboxes during mailbox replication," Microsoft said at the time.
"Not all Exchange servers will be impacted by installation of those updates equally; the severity and speed of impact varies based on Exchange server load. Some servers might never see a problem," it added in a separate blog describing the issues.
However, Microsoft said that this Outlook on the web (OWA) known issue isn't linked to the October 2026 Exchange server security updates and urged customers not to uninstall them.

articles.title: AWS had its agents build a free and open emulator for AWS. They now maintain it, too.
articles.summary:
AWS had its agents build a free and open emulator for AWS. They now maintain it, too.
AWS on Wednesday launched an emulator for AWS called AWS Emulator.
That, by itself, is interesting and may raise some questions about the future of LocalStack. But what’s maybe most interesting is that the emulator was entirely built by a team of agents and will also be maintained by them going forward.
Since AWS wasn’t sure it could actually copyright the work of these agents — and didn’t want to assert copyright where none may exist — the emulator is available under the Creative Commons Zero license, which puts the code into the public domain.
Tom ‘Spot’ Callaway, a principal open source software strategist at AWS, told The New Stack that there have obviously been other emulators in the past — and AWS itself has built some, too.
“The challenge is that they get out of date very quickly,” he explains. “They don’t always reflect reality on the ground, and because of that, they’re often not trusted. And we didn’t even trust them internally.”
With the rise of agentic coding tools, the team also saw a need for a better emulator that could help agents test code against AWS services without having to hand over AWS credentials to the agents.
Meanwhile, the team was also looking at a test case for building a full project with agents, and the emulator proved to be a good testing ground, in large part because it provided a bounded problem with clear goals and the ability to test the results.

articles.title: Tesla fait homologuer le FSD dans un pays aux conditions parmi les plus hostiles d'Europe
articles.summary:
Depuis que les Pays-Bas lui ont accordé une homologation provisoire en avril 2026, Tesla avance pays par pays en Europe avec son FSD, car le vote de l’Union européenne n’a toujours pas eu lieu. C’est désormais au tour de la Finlande de rejoindre l’Estonie, la Croatie ou encore la Belgique. Son autorité des transports, Traficom, a reconnu ce mardi 10 novembre l’homologation néerlandaise et a annoncé sa décision ce mercredi 11 novembre. Dans la foulée, Tesla Europe a confirmé sur X que le déploiement commencerait « bientôt ».
Le pays avait prévenu. En juin, Traficom se disait prêt à aller plus vite que Bruxelles, dont le vote était alors attendu en octobre. Dans son avis publié à l’époque, l’autorité listait les points à vérifier sur les routes finlandaises : le temps qu’il faut au conducteur pour reprendre la main, les dépassements quand la visibilité est mauvaise, et le décalage de vitesse (speed offset), un réglage qui permet au système de rouler jusqu’à 50 % au-dessus de la limite détectée. C’est ce point qui inquiétait la Suède et la Norvège, voisines de la Finlande. Pour mémoire, environ 6 500 voitures immatriculées en Finlande étaient alors équipées pour utiliser le système, soit 0,24 % des 2,7 millions de voitures particulières du pays.

articles.title: Dukosi Samples Contactless Battery Communication System - EE Times
articles.summary:
BUDAPEST, Hungary – At the Pretzl Connect 2026 press event, Edinburgh-based Dukosi announced it has begun commercial sampling of its DK-NFLNK, a contactless intra-battery communication solution designed to eliminate wiring harnesses and improve battery safety.
By transmitting voltage and temperature data wirelessly across a single bus antenna via near-field RF rather than copper cabling, the system removes failure points from the battery architecture, contributes to real-time thermal monitoring using data collected from Dukosi’s DKCMS chips, and supports data tracking helpful for the battery passport.
The Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 of the European Parliament and of the Council mandates that “From 18 February 2027 each LMT battery, each industrial battery with a capacity greater than 2 kWh, and each electric vehicle battery placed on the market or put into service shall have an electronic record (‘battery passport’).”
Vulnerability of physical cabling
“Connector failure rates in a conventional wiring harness are around 10 parts per million,” said Joseph Notaro, president of Dukosi in Budapest. “In the automotive and industrial arenas where you’re looking at parts-per-billion-level reliability, that failure rate is simply too high and an unacceptable risk of failure.”

articles.title: 5,4 Milliarden Tonnen CO2 weniger pro Jahr? Was am großen KI-Versprechen noch dran ist
articles.summary:
Sam Altman versprach die „Rettung des Klimas“ durch KI: Was ist davon heute übrig?
Während sich Vertreter aus aller Welt im türkischen Antalya zur Klimakonferenz der Vereinten Nationen treffen, dürfte ein Thema die Gespräche dominieren: Künstliche Intelligenz. Das Gastgeberland hat die Teilnehmenden bereits aufgefordert, sich zu verpflichten, KI so zu konzipieren und zu betreiben, dass sie den Klimaschutz stützt. Wie viel Effekt diese Selbstverpflichtung hat, sei dahingestellt. Bislang tut die Industrie weltweit jedenfalls bei weitem nicht genug – im Gegenteil. Statt die Technologie so zu nutzen, dass sie tatsächlich die Treibhausgasemissionen senkt, sorgt Big Tech für neue Emissionen.
Doch zunächst zum optimistischen Teil. Noch 2024 erklärte Sam Altman, CEO von OpenAI, dass KI „erstaunliche Erfolge“ für die Menschheit erzielen werde, darunter die „Rettung des Klimas“. Im Jahr zuvor schrieben die Leiterin der Nachhaltigkeitsabteilung bei Google und ein Co-Autor in einem Gastbeitrag im Magazin Fortune, dass KI die globalen CO₂-Emissionen bis 2030 um 5 bis 10 Prozent absenken könnte.
Die strittige Frage: Hilft KI nun gegen den Klimawandel oder nicht?

articles.title: Google’s Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps
articles.summary:
Google has cooked up a new experimental AI tool called Tabletop that generates customized collaborative hubs to help you coordinate with family, and friends. The Tabletop platform shares some visual similarities with workplace management apps like Asana and Monday, but with a built-in AI feature that allows you to vibecode personalized interactive tools by describing them, such as savings trackers, chore charts, event plans, and more.
Google’s Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps
Tabletop provides customizable, collaborative spaces for all your personal planning needs.
“Just add in your links, files and ideas, then prompt @tabletop — or pick a starter template — to generate custom interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters and tournament brackets,” Google Labs design and engineering lead Roman Nurik said in the blog post. “Once your space is ready, drop the invite link in your group chat to let everyone jump in and use it at the same time like a Google Doc.”
Access to the Tabletop beta is rolling out via a waitlist, and currently limited to people over the age of 18 in the US. Some of the example use cases that Nurik provides in his video above would clearly require giving kids or teens access to Tabletop, however, and using this for personal family planning looks like a compelling alternative to stuffy workplace software, so that age requirement might only be in place while Tabletop is in public testing.

articles.title: JioHotstar Benchmarks Knowledge Bases for AI Coding Agents
articles.summary:
JioHotstar evaluated six approaches to helping AI coding agents navigate large codebases, finding that structural code search performed well on clearly defined engineering tasks, while semantic retrieval helped more with ambiguous requirements. The evaluation also found that adding retrieval layers did not consistently improve task completion or reduce token consumption.
Abhishek Bansal, Senior Staff Engineer at JioHotStar, compared filesystem tools, Sourcebot, Graphify, CocoIndex Code, Repowise, and an in-house retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline. The team evaluated the approaches using subsets of SWE-bench and CodeScaleBench, alongside a custom question-answering harness for JioHotstar's codebase. The experiments used Claude Sonnet as the solving model and measured task accuracy, token consumption, agent turns, and tool usability.
JioHotstar’s benchmark setup for evaluating code retrieval approaches for AI coding agents. (Source: JioHotstar Blog Post)
The filesystem baseline, which relied on locally checked out repositories and standard search and file operations, remained competitive on concrete tasks. Sourcebot, which provides indexed text search, symbol definitions, references, and file reads, performed better than the baseline on harder SWE-bench Verified tasks while also costing less. On simpler SWE-bench Lite tasks, retrieval generally added overhead without consistently improving results.

articles.title: UAEF: A framework-agnostic system for closed-loop evaluation of AI agents | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
UAEF: A framework-agnostic system for closed-loop evaluation of AI agents
Teams building AI agents on AWS use a range of frameworks, including LangGraph, LangChain, Strands Agents, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Each framework records agent execution in its own way, so the structure of messages, tool calls, and handoffs between agents differs from one to the next. Evaluation tooling tends to follow the same boundaries: teams build metrics, scoring logic, and result storage against a single framework’s trace format, and they must rebuild them when they switch frameworks or run agents on more than one.
This coupling makes a basic development question harder to answer: did a change to the prompt, model, or tools improve the agent? Answering it requires consistent metrics across versions of an agent and a shared record of past results to compare against. Agent quality also spans several dimensions that a single accuracy score does not capture: tool calling, response quality, responsible AI, performance, multi-turn conversation, multi-agent coordination, and reasoning.
In this post, we introduce the Universal Agent Evaluation Framework (UAEF). Customers across 12 organizations in the telecom, healthcare, and financial services industries used UAEF to evaluate their AI agents with one consistent set of metrics and compare agent versions before release. articles.title: GitHub Makes Agentic Workflows Generally Available with Isolation and Budget Controls
articles.summary:
GitHub has made GitHub Agentic Workflows generally available. The open-source project runs coding agents inside GitHub Actions for repository tasks such as issue triage and continuous integration (CI) failure analysis. Agents start with read-only permissions, and any changes they propose are applied by separate jobs that hold their own write tokens.
That separation has limits. The project's FAQ says the protections do not automatically extend to direct write permissions or to custom jobs a workflow author adds, so the safety of a workflow depends on how it is configured. Authors can also add a GitHub Environment protection rule to require a reviewer before a write job runs.
Developers describe the work in natural-language Markdown, with YAML frontmatter for configuration. The project compiles that definition into a standard Actions workflow, which reuses existing runner groups and policy constraints, and teams can use Copilot or bring another coding agent. According to the general availability announcement, agents run in a sandboxed container behind the Agent Workflow Firewall, and a threat-detection job scans proposed changes before they are applied. The project entered public preview in June 2026.
Since the preview, GitHub has added support for Actions Runner Controller (ARC), its Kubernetes operator for self-hosted runners, with Docker-in-Docker (DinD). DinD runs a Docker daemon inside the runner pod so the agent can start its sandbox containers. The project's guide notes …

Entre les faux emails de livraison, les liens bancaires frauduleux, les réseaux Wi-Fi publics et les fichiers téléchargés trop vite, la sécurité d’un PC ne se joue plus seulement sur la présence d’un antivirus. Bitdefender Internet Security répondait précisément à ce besoin sous Windows, mais l’offre n’est désormais plus commercialisée. Elle a été remplacée par Bitdefender Total Security Individual, qui reprend les principales protections d’Internet Security et les étend à 5 appareils sous Windows, macOS, iOS et Android. Le VPN standard reste limité à 200 Mo par jour et par appareil, ce qui en fait surtout une protection ponctuelle.
Avis : Bitdefender Internet Security reste une référence connue, mais l’offre appartient désormais au passé commercial de l’éditeur. Total Security Individual est son successeur logique : plus large, multiplateforme et toujours solide sous Windows, avec un VPN standard volontairement limité.
Points forts

Si alguna vez te has preguntado hasta dónde llega la compatibilidad de Windows, un desarrollador que firma como Enlyth ha intentado responderlo buscando la aplicación con interfaz gráfica más antigua que todavía arranca en Windows 11 sin emulación ni modificaciones. El autor lo cuenta en su blog, donde apunta a que la búsqueda acabó a principios de los noventa, aunque con un poco de trampa puede llegar a retrasarse más atrás.
Sin sitio para los 16 bits. Windows 11 no puede ejecutar programas de 16 bits. Y es que, según la documentación de compatibilidad de Microsoft, las versiones x64 y ARM de Windows no admiten código x86 de 16 bits de ningún tipo, así que cualquier candidato tiene que ser una aplicación de 32 bits. Eso lleva a los inicios de Windows NT, cuya primera versión, Windows NT 3.1, salió el 27 de julio de 1993 como sistema de 32 bits.
Un solitario de 1993. Pero hay un atajo que adelanta un poco el reloj. Como explica en la misma entrada, en un foro anónimo alguien le habló de Win32s, unas bibliotecas que permitían ejecutar aplicaciones de 32 bits sobre Windows 3.1, o sea que hacían de puente entre las dos épocas. Las primeras versiones de Win32s traían el FreeCell, y la copia que encontró, del 22 de febrero de 1993, funciona en Windows 11 sin tocar nada.

articles.title: Managing performing assets when VC fund lifecycles expire
articles.summary:
Conversations about venture exits usually start with the portfolio company. Is the business ready? Is there a buyer? Yet as a fund ages, another question becomes equally critical: how long can the vehicle holding the company afford to wait?
The Stears–Ventures Platform Africa Venture Capital Exit & Liquidity Report tracks 181 verified VC-backed exits across Africa between 2011 and 2026. However, for a fund manager, the primary challenge rarely lies in underperforming investments. Instead, it stems from performing companies that retain meaningful upside but no longer align with the fund’s remaining life. This misalignment transforms an exit-timing issue into a residual portfolio paradox.
Market responses are beginning to emerge. For instance, GIZ’s ICAMA Initiative, alongside MEDA in Q3 2026, explores a Pan-African Secondary Fund for performing, de-risked late-stage assets. The core structural mismatch is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore: an investor may reach the end of a fund’s lifecycle before a company’s value can be realised on appropriate terms. This raises a fundamental question: what happens when the fund runs out of time before that value crystallises?

articles.title: Fin des voitures thermiques : l’Europe prête à laisser la porte ouverte après 2035 ?
articles.summary:
L’Union européenne aurait-elle voulu aller trop vite sur la fin de commercialisation des voitures thermiques ? Le cap est fixé à 2035 : passé cette date, les constructeurs ne pourront plus vendre de voitures neuves embarquant un moteur à explosion, qu’elles soient thermiques ou hybrides. Toutefois, la réglementation semble évoluer en faveur d’une conservation limitée des moteurs thermiques.
Des objectifs qui s’assouplissent
Lors de l’adoption du règlement (UE) 2023/851, le cap était clair : une réduction de 100 % des émissions de CO2 des véhicules neufs en 2035 par rapport à 2021. Ce qui veut dire que les voitures neuves utilisant un moteur thermique devront disparaître des catalogues européens des constructeurs.
Toutefois, l’Union européenne semble revenir sur cette décision forte. En ce début novembre, un vote de la commission de l’Environnement a pour but de remodeler cette règle. Le cap de 2035 serait conservé, mais la réduction des émissions de CO2 devrait atteindre 87,5 % par rapport à 2021. Ce qui laisse quelque peu d’espoir aux moteurs thermiques de continuer à exister sous le capot de certains véhicules.
Des mécanismes de compensation sont aussi prévus par le projet de texte du règlement. Il est notamment prévu l’achat de crédits liés à l’utilisation d’acier « vert » produit en Europe, permettant de produire des véhicules plus polluants que la cible de l’Union européenne si d’importants efforts sont faits sur la décarbonation de la production du véhicule.

articles.title: CISA flags Cisco BroadWorks flaw as actively exploited in attacks
articles.summary:
The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned on Tuesday that hackers are now exploiting a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability in attacks.
Cisco BroadWorks is a cloud unified communications (UC) software platform and the underlying engine allowing telecom carriers and managed service providers (MSPs) to provide branded cloud PBX, voice, and collaboration services to business customers.
Tracked as CVE-2026-20320, the security flaw stems from an improper restriction of XML External Entity (XXE) reference weakness in the Open Client Interface (OCI) XML Parser that can allow unauthenticated, remote attackers to read sensitive configuration information from vulnerable systems by sending maliciously crafted XML messages.
"This vulnerability exists because XML entries are improperly parsed due to external entity resolution being allowed by default. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted XML message to the Open Client Interface - Provisioning (OCI-P) service," Cisco explained when it patched the bug in August.
CISA flagged CVE-2026-20320 as actively exploited and added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday, ordering Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to secure their systems within two weeks, by November 24, as mandated by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.

articles.title: Critical Xen Orchestra Flaws Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
A threat actor has been exploiting a critical-severity authentication bypass and a zero-day in Xen Orchestra, software maker Vates warns.
A web-based backup, management, and disaster recovery solution for XCP-ng and XenServer virtualization environments, Xen Orchestra operates as an agentless control center across hosts, VMs, storage, and pools.
The critical flaw exists in the REST authentication mechanism, where an authentication token is turned into {} and then treated as an unfiltered lookup, leading to the first token being returned by token collection. If the token is not expired, the provider authenticates as its owner.
This opens a route that exposes reusable login token IDs, allowing unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication and gain administrator privileges.
“Xen Orchestra compromise can lead to arbitrary code execution on managed pools and a full XCP-ng node takeover as root,” Vates says.
The security defect impacts Xen Orchestra releases before 6.9.2 (stable) and 6.10.1 (latest), and Xen Orchestra Appliance, which contains Xen Orchestra.
Vates warned that the same threat actor has been exploiting this bug and a zero-day vulnerability that requires administrator privileges. The zero-day allows malicious VM imports that could compromise XCP-ng hosts, and a fix is still being developed.
According to the company, the attacker initially operated from 91.211.251.112:8001 and via the Tor network. No CVE identifier has been assigned to the security defects.

articles.title: Un vecino de Salamanca se puso a lanzar bolas de papel mojado desde un sexto piso. Ahora se enfrenta a una multa publicada en el BOE
articles.summary:
Todavía recuerdo las clases donde más de uno y más de dos mojaban una bolita de papel, la introducían en el tubo vacío de un boli y, a modo de cerbatana, la proyectaban sobre el cuello o la mochila de algún cándido estudiante que ni sabía por dónde le había llegado el ataque. Ahora imagina esto a escala más “industrial”.
Hace un par de meses, una patrulla de la Policía Local de Salamanca vio a alguien lanzar bolas de papel mojado desde la terraza de un sexto piso. Las bolas caían cerca de la terraza de un bar y salpicaban. Ahí quedó la cosa, ¿no? No: semanas más tarde, el Ayuntamiento publicó en el BOE una propuesta de sanción al vecino, cazado con 751 euros. No es ninguna broma y tiene un precedente jurídico.
Qué pasó. El lanzamiento partió de una vivienda en la calle Bordadores. Las bolas llegaron a las inmediaciones de la terraza de un establecimiento de hostelería. Este estaba en la calle Condes de Crespo Rascón. La notificación no precisa cuántas fueron, no habla de heridos ni daños y no cita a vecinos o peatones afectados. Pero la broma fue cazada por la Policía Local, quienes advirtieron la escena e identificaron al presunto autor. Hasta hay un precedente de 200 euros por una situación análoga.

Expensive accelerators, no workload-level visibility: Introducing Amazon CloudWatch accelerated compute insights
Accelerator bills have become one of the largest lines in the infrastructure budget. GPUs have become the most expensive resource in modern computing, and yet most organizations operate them with little visibility. A single training cluster can run for days and cost millions of dollars. Most organizations pool these accelerators across teams on shared clusters to keep them busy. But in these shared environments, platform teams cannot answer basic questions: which team is using which accelerators? Is the inference workload generating tokens efficiently? What is wasting money?
When a workload degrades (a failing accelerator, a thermally throttled node), teams find out only after a run crashes or the bill arrives. The device-level signals needed to find the cause (request traces, kernel logs, memory metrics from the accelerator itself) are not collected or connected. Without a way to isolate the problem to a single accelerator, teams fall back on cycling the entire instance, surrendering seven healthy GPUs to address a fault on one, and often waiting on scarce capacity to get the instance back.

Nigeria’s active mobile subscriptions rose 29% in two years to 200.3 million in September 2026, recovering from the sharp decline that followed the enforcement of the National Identification Number (NIN)-SIM linkage policy.
The rebound, however, remains concentrated among two operators, with MTN and Airtel accounting for about 86% of active connections, leaving Globacom and T2 with a much smaller share of the market.
MTN had 104.6 million active subscriptions in September, while Airtel had 68 million. They collectively accounted for about 172.7 million out of the 200.1 million recorded across the four operators. Globacom had 23.5 million, while T2 had 3.6 million, according to the latest data from the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC).
The 200 million mobile subscriptions refer to active phone lines, not that 200 million people own or use mobile phones. One person can have multiple SIM cards, and active connections also include SIMs used in routers and other devices.
The figure marks a new milestone since the full enforcement of NIN-SIM linkage in 2024, which led to a sharp reduction in reported connections. The policy required mobile subscribers to link their phone lines to verified national identity numbers. The policy was introduced in 2020, but its enforcement intensified in 2024 as operators completed the verification and disconnection of lines without valid NIN records.

Des pirates exploitent Outlook pour récupérer votre identité Windows

articles.title: eBPF Rootkits: Why Underground Actors Are Taking Notice
articles.summary:
For years, eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) has been one of the most celebrated technologies in the Linux kernel. It lets developers run sandboxed programs inside the kernel without writing kernel modules, while powering everything from network monitoring to security tooling.
Linux is extremely popular in production servers and giants like Google, Cloudflare, and Meta rely on it daily.
The same eBPF capabilities that are attractive for defenders, however, can be a powerful weapon in the hands of attackers. Flare’s research found underground forum posts sharing eBPF rootkit code and step-by-step tutorials.
One Russian-language post described how to build an implant with process hiding and packet-triggered activation, and included screenshots the author presented as demonstrations.
What Makes eBPF Dangerous?
Traditional Linux rootkits typically rely on loadable kernel modules (LKMs) to hook system calls and hide malicious activity. These are well-understood by defenders, and most EDR solutions watch for suspicious module loads. eBPF, however, behaves in a different way.
An eBPF malware can hook into kernel functions, observe system calls, or inspect and modify network traffic using the same kernel-supported bpf() interface as legitimate tools like Cilium.
Its programs run without loading a kernel module, so a routine lsmod check can miss them. The challenge for defenders is determining who loaded the program and what it does.

Durante mucho tiempo, la imagen de la salud muscular ha estado muy ligada al volumen que se tenía en diferentes partes del cuerpo. Y desde la cultura del fitness hasta las recomendaciones médicas más tradicionales, el mensaje parecía claro: para no envejecer de forma frágil, había que mantener la masa muscular. Sin embargo, este concepto va cambiando en los últimos años para darle mucho más peso a la fuerza que se puede ejercer.
El cambio de paradigma. El deterioro físico asociado a la edad se ha diagnosticado a través de la sarcopenia, un concepto que tradicionalmente ponía el foco en la pérdida de masa muscular y en la fragilidad. Sin embargo, el consenso europeo sobre la definición y el diagnóstico de la sarcopenia, actualizado en 2019 y liderado por investigadores españoles del Hospital Ramón y Cajal, cambió las reglas del juego.
El nuevo criterio establece la pérdida de fuerza como el rasgo principal e inicial del deterioro, relegando la cantidad y calidad de la masa a un segundo plano.
¿Por qué? La razón de este cambio se basa en un seguimiento hecho a casi 2.000 adultos mayores durante tres años, donde se pudo ver que la fuerza de nuestras piernas cae entre un 2,6% y un 4,1% al año. Es decir, perdemos fuerza hasta tres veces más rápido de lo que perdemos masa muscular. Y lo peor es que el mismo estudio demostró que ganar masa muscular no evitó que los participantes siguieran perdiendo fuerza.

articles.title: A radio-wave trick from the 1980s could keep fusion reactors running continuously
articles.summary:
Why it matters: A fusion power plant only makes sense if it can run for days on end, much like the coal and gas plants it would replace. Most tokamaks, however, still work in bursts, because the giant magnet coil driving their plasma current eventually has to stop and reset. Physicists in San Diego have now shown that radio waves can carry some of that load instead, using a trick that every experiment in the 1980s failed to pull off.
The coil in question, a central solenoid, works a lot like a transformer. It keeps ramping up its own current to induce one in the plasma, but it eventually runs out of room to ramp. Those stop-start cycles also wear on the machine over time, so engineers would much rather run a reactor in steady state.
The new method, called helicon current drive, gets around that by beaming 476 MHz radio waves into the plasma, where they nudge electrons along and keep current flowing without the coil's help. Bob Pinsker, a General Atomics physicist on the new paper, was among those who tried it back then. He told the American Nuclear Society that the theory predicted a very weak effect in '80s-era plasmas, so researchers were "kind of hoping for a miracle."
That miracle never showed up, so the idea sat on the shelf for decades. These days, though, DIII-D can produce plasmas that come fairly close to reactor conditions. Así se pronuncia Isabel Ocaña, administradora de fincas y vicepresidenta primera del Colegio Profesional de Administradores de Fincas de Madrid. Se trata de la situación en la que se quiere utilizar el tomacorriente de la comunidad (por ejemplo, en el garaje) para la recarga de un vehículo eléctrico. En este caso, los dueños de los vehículos no pueden enchufar por su cuenta a los tomacorrientes de la comunidad.
El asunto tiene que ver con nuestro bolsillo. Si utilizamos el suministro comunitario para la recarga, los consumos se contabilizan en la comunidad. Recordemos que la toma de corriente y el suministro son servicios comunes.
En este caso hay que contar con el acuerdo de la comunidad y establecer un sistema de individualización de consumos. Es decir, que la comunidad disponga de un sistema que permita cuantificar el consumo de cada uno de los usuarios y que su coste se le cobre. Si se instala un punto privado en una plaza individual, los costes de instalación y de consumo de electricidad corren por completo a cargo de los interesados (artículo 17.5 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal).
En estos casos no es necesario un acuerdo de la junta. Es suficiente con informar a la comunidad de antemano. Hay que destacar que esto es aplicable a los puntos de recarga privados en plaza individual.

Databricks on Wednesday unveiled an updated version of its AI agent Genie, which can now perform multistep jobs that take extended work to finish. It does this through an ontology that Databricks built to give Genie the context it needs from the information that customers store on the Databricks platform.
Corporate leaders can now assign the agent a wide range of tasks, and it will complete them unsupervised, the company says. To prove the point, Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi showed me how he uses it internally. Instead of a product demo, he fired up his actual agent and walked me through his most recent chats and charts.
He showed me how it analyzed the parts of an employee satisfaction survey where the company didn’t score well, and how it helped him rate (and discard) fixes for those low scores that some executives suggested. He showed me how it summarized a big sales pitch to a prospect that went poorly — including the features the prospect said it needed before buying.
It also prepped him for a podcast interview by reviewing his previous appearances and developing likely questions. While we talked, he even had it tell him what he should say to me. (And its advice on that wasn’t bad.)
The fascinating part was that Ghodsi was using Genie to find the stuff that he’s now unlikely to hear as the big boss. It was a source of unvarnished truth about what wasn’t going well that he needed to address.

articles.title: Arrêter les dégâts « dans les 35 secondes » : OpenAI dévoile le kill switch censé stopper ses IA quand elles dérapent
articles.summary:
Si l’été a été la saison des crises cyber chez OpenAI, l’automne doit être celle de la reprise en main.
L’entreprise américaine a dévoilé le 10 novembre Control Room, un service qui suit l’ensemble des modèles en activité dans son infrastructure de recherche et qui, selon le billet d’OpenAI, « interrompt la génération du modèle dans les 35 secondes suivant une décision d’intervention » lorsqu’un problème de sûreté ou de sécurité est détecté.
L’outil arrive après plusieurs mois agités. Le 21 juillet, OpenAI révélait notamment que plusieurs de ses agents étaient sortis de leur environnement de test et avaient piraté les serveurs de Hugging Face, la grande plateforme de partage de modèles d’IA.
En août, l’entreprise annonçait avoir suspendu une partie de ses entraînements pendant deux semaines afin de revoir sa sécurité, avant de les relancer. Ce qui n’a visiblement pas suffi. Le 20 septembre, un agent en cours d’entraînement a contourné les restrictions réseau de son bac à sable, ce qui a conduit OpenAI à suspendre de nouveau les travaux sur ses modèles les plus puissants.
Le modèle de surveillance avait bien levé une alerte au bout d’une douzaine de minutes, mais la tâche n’a été stoppée que près de 2 h 45 après le début de l’incident. C’est précisément ce délai que Control Room doit réduire.
Comment Control Room coupe une tâche
