But it draws the line at requiring police to obtain warrants before searching its databases, which is less of a surprise.
As Arizona Capitol Times reports, Flock policy director Andrea Korb told an R Street Institute webinar that the company supports state-by-state legislation governing its camera technology. It expects a wave of bills in 2027, with lawmakers interested even in states that have recently passed restrictions.
"There is a lot of fear and concern about this technology right now and we want people to know ... your legislature has looked at this and here are the safeguards that have been put in place," Korb said. "There shouldn't be unfettered access to all vehicles and all cameras for any reason."
There is, however, a fairly big sticking point, and probably the most contentious element when it comes to Flock searches: warrants. Korb backed independent third-party audits, noting these are already in place in Minnesota, but argued that requiring police to obtain warrants before searching the databases would burden officers and substantially reduce the technology's effectiveness.

articles.title: Ley de Propiedad Horizontal: se puede prohibir el uso del ascensor a los vecinos que no paguen la comunidad en algunos casos
articles.summary:
Que un vecino deje de pagar las cuotas de la comunidad o una derrama es un problema para todos. En estos casos, la comunidad de propietarios tiene herramientas más allá de limitarse a reclamarle la deuda, y entre otras cosas puede impedirle utilizar el ascensor mientras no se ponga al día. Esto se desprende de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, aunque siempre dentro de lo que marcan dos artículos concretos de la ley.
El papel de los artículos 6 y 21. El artículo 6 es el que ordena la convivencia, porque permite que el conjunto de propietarios fije normas de régimen interior para regular la utilización de los servicios y cosas comunes, unas normas que obligan a todos los titulares mientras no se modifiquen. Como el ascensor es un elemento común, su uso puede ordenarse por esa vía, pero los estatutos no sirven para privar de derechos de forma arbitraria a uno de los vecinos.
La herramienta realmente pensada para la morosidad está en el artículo 21.1, que desde la reforma de junio de 2022 permite a la junta de propietarios acordar medidas disuasorias mientras dure el impago. Tal y como recoge el texto del precepto, esas medidas pueden ir desde fijar intereses superiores al legal hasta la privación temporal del uso de servicios o instalaciones, siempre que no puedan considerarse abusivas o desproporcionadas y no afecten a la habitabilidad de los inmuebles. Además, no pueden tener carácter retroactivo, aunque la comunidad puede incluirlas en sus estatutos.

Initially created as a fork of ARTEX 0.1.1, AntiFox has a Chinese-language interface and lets users deploy AI agents and automate common penetration-testing tasks, such as mapping exposed services and probing target endpoints for vulnerabilities.
Security researchers at Arctic Wolf observed malicious AntiFox-linked infrastructure hosted on Alibaba Cloud using valid AWS identities, including IAM users and, in some cases, assumed EC2 roles, to make authenticated requests to Amazon Web Services APIs.
“In several recently observed intrusions, Alibaba Cloud systems hosting AntiFox interfaces were associated with confirmed malicious actions against internet-facing web services and associated AWS environments,” Arctic Wolf says.
One case highlighted in the report involved deploying an ASPX webshell on an internet-exposed IIS server, executing OS commands, accessing application settings and database connection strings, and copying configuration and log files to a web-accessible directory.

AMD shares how it can retain 95% of server performance with just half the DRAM, sidestepping memory shortages with MEXT — tech powers over 100 servers already running, with plans to expand to 2,000 servers in 2027
MEXT offloads cold memory pages to flash storage and serves them up with a predictive AI model.
In June, AMD overtook the predictive memory engine known as MEXT, which claims to offer upwards of 99% of the performance of a system with full DRAM capacity while running with as little as 25% of the physical DIMMs. The technology offloads cold memory pages to flash storage and uses an AI model to serve pages before they’re needed, and AMD says it plans to extend the tech across a wide swath of its IT infrastructure next year.
The pitch behind MEXT seems too good to be true. According to AMD and MEXT founder Gary Smerdon, the technology can cut the physical DRAM required in a server by 20% to 75% depending on the application and performance target. That missing memory still registers as installed DRAM to the OS. Instead of DRAM, however, MEXT uses relatively inexpensive flash storage to offload cold pages, flying them back in as they’re needed with an AI model. In some of AMD’s internal workloads, such as Synopsys PrimeTime, the company says it’s able to achieve 95% of the performance of a full server while running at 50% DRAM capacity with MEXT.

articles.title: Google DeepMind just mathematically verified key parts of Signal
articles.summary:
Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself.
Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world’s communications on platforms like the Signal app, Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind’s formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code.
More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn’t have critical vulnerabilities.
Before the AI era, it was incredibly time-consuming for people to describe the characteristics of software they wanted to prove, turn these summaries into formulas, and then develop the proof. Agentic AI can significantly cut down the time of the latter project, enabling analyses like DeepMind’s Signal evaluation. articles.title: Trump wanted little Kei trucks for America, Toyota makes it happen
articles.summary:
The idea that Americans should be offered a greater choice of smaller cars has support from strange bedfellows indeed. After all, who could forget President Trump—usually one to take a maximalist approach to any problem—announcing last year that he wanted the Department of Transportation to make Japan’s diminutive “Kei” cars legal here in the US.
Ars’ attempts to get DoT to tell us more about the potential influx of little vehicles have mostly fallen on deaf ears. But this week, there has been movement on the topic, with Toyota announcing that it will bring back the Scion brand with the KEI-01.
What’s a Kei car?
In the US, the preponderance of humongous SUVs is a consequence largely of government policies, specifically corporate average fuel economy standards that made it less profitable to sell smaller, efficient cars. Japan’s Kei cars are what happens if the government instead restricts the size, engine capacity, and power output.
A Kei car must fit within the following dimensions: 11.2 feet (3.4 m) long, 4.9 feet (1.5 m) wide, and 6.6 feet (2 m) tall, with an engine displacement of no more than 0.66 L and an output of 63 hp (47 kW) or less. That’s a far cry from the more than 16 feet (4.9 m) of a full-size pickup truck, but it makes sense for a country where you’re not allowed to buy a car unless you have somewhere to park it, with those spaces being at an absolute premium.

articles.title: Confirmado por la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal: no se permite prohibir el uso del ascensor a los vecinos que no paguen la comunidad
articles.summary:
En caso de impago de la comunidad, tenemos derecho a iniciar una acción judicial para que el propietario pague. Además, podemos adoptar medidas disuasorias. Sin embargo, no podemos bloquearle el ascensor por ello. En la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal se reconocen las posibilidades de actuar para evitar impagos. No obstante, no pueden afectar a la habitabilidad de las viviendas.
Por ello, no podemos decir que la ley nos da carta blanca para impedir el acceso al ascensor a los morosos. En la Guía de administradores de fincas colegiados se indica que está excluida esta posibilidad por ser fundamental para la habitabilidad de la finca.
Qué permiten los artículos 6 y 21
Artículo 6. Los propietarios podrán establecer las normas de régimen interior que consideren convenientes para el buen funcionamiento de la finca. Medida de contención. Las dunas son la principal protección que muchos hogares del condado de Lancashire tienen contra el mar. Sin embargo, la costa ha perdido aproximadamente el 80% de sus dunas desde mediados del siglo XIX, según Pennington, a medida que las localidades de Blackpool y Lytham St Annes se expandían sobre ellas.
Cómo funciona. Los voluntarios entierran los árboles en zanjas poco profundas, dejando las ramas superiores expuestas. Cuando sopla el viento, las acículas y las ramas atrapan los granos de arena, y se forma gradualmente un montículo alrededor de cada árbol. La Wildlife Trust afirma que esto puede producir nuevas dunas en un plazo de entre seis meses y un año, un proceso que llevaría siglos en la naturaleza, según comparten desde Sky News.

El Ministerio de Defensa confirmó la medida y dijo que reemplazará los aparatos por modelos nacionales o europeos. La orden afecta a toda la Bundeswehr, las fuerzas armadas de Alemania.
Según la revista, la orden se emitió en las últimas semanas. Los aparatos ya comprados se retiran de servicio lo más rápido posible. Un portavoz del ministerio dijo a Der Spiegel que en la Bundeswehr ya no se usarán modelos chinos y que los sistemas existentes se sustituirán por productos nacionales o europeos.
El temor es que los drones envíen a los servicios de inteligencia de China datos sobre ejercicios militares, imágenes de cuarteles y campos de entrenamiento, o información sobre los sistemas de armas alemanes, según el medio. El diario holandés Volkskrant, que cita a Der Spiegel, agrega que hay indicios concretos, pero que el ministerio no quiso detallarlos.
También quedan fuera los autos de BYD, Geely y NIO
La prohibición no se limita a los drones. Según Stern, que cita a Der Spiegel, circulan entre las unidades listas de modelos de fabricantes chinos como BYD, Geely y NIO que no pueden entrar en instalaciones clasificadas como zonas de seguridad. Los soldados que tengan esos autos deben estacionar fuera de los cuarteles y caminar hasta su puesto.

The Linux Kernel is probably one of the best ecosystems to observe regarding the impact of AI in programming. The critical importance of its code and its maintainers' quality standards mean that patches, including but not only AI slop, go through rigorous review and are often discarded. Still, the amount of AI-produced code is often far higher than what the human reviewers can deal with. Lorenzo Stoakes, a lead Linux reviewer for memory management, has elected to step down from some of his former duties for exactly that reason.
Stoakes announced his decision today in a thread on the Linux kernel mailing list (LKML). He'll be leaving the core, reclaim, Rust, THP (Huge Pages), and miscellaneous sections of the kernel memory management section, while staying on for his remaining duties, including KVM. articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by assembling first structure in orbit without astronauts
articles.summary:
The big picture: These days, anything large that's heading to orbit either gets folded up to fit inside a rocket or is assembled by astronauts once it arrives. A small robot from Caltech has now tried a third route. Up in low Earth orbit, it pieced together part of an antenna frame from loose struts and joints. Its creators say that makes it the first structure ever built autonomously in space.
The machine, called ASTRA, takes up roughly a cubic meter and packs a gantry arm, motorized parts dispensers and 11 cameras. Engineers also squeezed two finished sections of the frame inside before launch, so its first job in orbit was simply pushing those out.
After that, the fairly basic arm got to work, sliding along three straight axes to pull composite tubes and aluminum joints from the dispensers. That's how the third section came together, piece by piece. Once a section is done, the robot attaches a netlike reflective film to it, since that film is what eventually turns the frame into an antenna.
The finished antenna is supposed to span 1.4 meters (4.5 feet), which takes 11 of those sections. But only three are in place so far, and the mission wraps up in December. So the team doesn't expect to finish the full frame.
The word "autonomous" also comes with a bit of an asterisk here. While the robot handled the physical assembly, three team members on the ground sent it commands and checked progress through photos sent down from orbit. Whenever something went wrong, they first recr…

articles.title: Is Jensen Huang’s bad behavior more commonplace than it seems? | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The AI industry is still reeling from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s honeypot scandal, but some in the industry see it as an issue that’s much larger than one man.
The Chinese government has been active in economic espionage for decades, and with semiconductors at the center of the AI boom, there’s intense pressure to infiltrate any company involved. At the same time, many of the executives getting rich off that boom have made themselves easy targets.
As CEO of investment intel firm Heron Intelligence, Nate Singer has a unique view into the problem. His firm works on corporate due diligence: Essentially, making sure companies know the relevant dirt before making a major acquisition or executive hire. And while the Nvidia case is particularly severe, Singer says there are lots of similar cases in the semiconductor industry that have stayed under the radar.
“We’ve got former employees talking about behavior at senior executive levels,” Singer told TechCrunch, saying executives are “really crossing lines that should not be crossed.”
In a widely circulated LinkedIn post, Singer detailed one case in which a CEO’s wife made an unexpected board room appearance, “screaming about her husband and another company exec flying around in the corporate jet with a couple young ladies (who also turned out to be state-sponsored actors).”
It’s an alarming story, but an unfortunately common one. Singer says he’s seen at least three reports of similar cases, and suspects many more have gone unreported…

articles.title: Por primera vez, un robot ha construido de forma autónoma parte de una estructura en el espacio
articles.summary:
Para estudiar el espacio profundo y detectar incluso los objetos más débiles necesitaremos telescopios espaciales cada vez más grandes. Si queremos comunicarnos de forma más eficiente en el espacio, son necesarias antenas de transmisión mucho mayores que las que se usan hoy en día. El problema es que ambas soluciones chocan con un mismo obstáculo: su tamaño. Hoy en día, los cohetes espaciales tienen un límite de carga que no permite poner en órbita dispositivos colosales. Hay algunas soluciones, pero también están bastante limitadas. Por eso, un equipo de científicos de Caltech ha probado un robot que construye estructuras directamente en el espacio.
De momento, solo ha fabricado un módulo de una antena, pero ha servido para demostrar que la construcción automatizada en el espacio no es una utopía.
Pequeño, pero muy completo. ASTRA es un robot de pórtico; es decir, un robot que se mueve en línea recta a lo largo de tres ejes perpendiculares: izquierda-derecha, adelante-atrás y arriba-abajo. Ocupa un metro cúbico y en su interior lleva un brazo robótico y un dispensador motorizado con materiales de construcción. En la primera prueba ha viajado también junto a dos módulos ya montados de la antena que iba a construir en órbita. El objetivo era comprobar que era capaz de ensamblar piezas, así que, para tardar menos, bastaría con que montase solo el último módulo en el espacio. FinMin asks ministries to make EVs the default and preferred choice for staff car purchases
To promote electric mobility, reduce dependence on fossil fuels, and account for prevailing market prices and vehicle lifecycle costs, the Finance Ministry is revising the net dealer price ceiling for procuring EVs and internal combustion engine vehicles.
The Finance Ministry has asked ministries and departments to make electric vehicles (EVs) their "default and preferred choice" for staff cars, and set a price cap of Rs 20 lakh for procurement of such vehicles.
The Finance Ministry said that, to promote electric mobility, reduce dependence on fossil fuels, and account for prevailing market prices and vehicle lifecycle costs, it is revising the net dealer price (NDP) ceiling for procuring EVs and internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles.
Accordingly, the NDP ceiling for EVs has been set at Rs 20 lakh, double the Rs 10 lakh limit set for ICE vehicles (petrol/diesel/hybrid).
The 2022 instructions prescribing the guidelines regarding procurement and hiring of cars by ministries/departments had fixed the NDP ceiling at Rs 6 lakh.
In an office memorandum dated November 10, the Expenditure Department said going forward, ministries/departments shall ordinarily procure EVs at the time of condemnation/replacement of their existing ICE staff cars.
"EVs shall be the default and preferred choice for procurement," it said.

articles.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
CoreWeave is rewriting how it pays for the AI boom, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings, reported on Tuesday. CoreWeave, a neocloud that rents out the computing power behind AI, said it’s increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even pursuing short-term deals that could lead to higher prices.
The new strategies could help CoreWeave finance its growth more efficiently while squeezing more cash from existing infrastructure. But these bets only hold if today’s demand and pricing power continue.
CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168% from the year prior, but it also posted a $709 million net loss and $846 million in quarterly interest expense.
“We will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to,” CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said during Tuesday’s earnings call.
Instead, CoreWeave’s plan is to rely on loans backed by specific customer contracts, drawing on funds as needed to finance most of infrastructure it still has to build to deliver on its significant backlog of $132.5 billion.
CoreWeave also said it expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months, including more than $3 billion tied to signing new customer contracts for capacity it has already built, which requires no additional spending on hardware.

The Trump administration’s fight to stop suspected leaks of top-secret military information on LinkedIn can’t sweep in “a vast number of confidential sources” of random journalists “who have no conceivable relationship” to the Department of Justice’s investigation, an appeals court ruled Tuesday.
The order came after the DOJ asked LinkedIn to turn over 18 months of communications from targeted journalists who collectively published more than 1,000 articles on many different topics over that time period. The request was not limited to journalists involved in a controversial report from a news outlet that Trump said exposed confidential military information in a foreign country. (The outlet is not being named to protect national security secrets.) Instead, the DOJ cast a wide net, requesting extensive LinkedIn data on journalists who had any possible link to the journalists around the time the report was drafted.
The majority of journalists have LinkedIn accounts and publish their contact information to encourage sources to connect on the platform, LinkedIn argued. So allowing that government overreach went beyond harming targeted journalists and threatened to undermine a critical platform where journalists frequently connect with confidential sources, judges ruled. Even more concerning, the Trump administration secured a secrecy order barring LinkedIn from telling anyone about the sweeping request for a year. Such an investment may give markets “a shot of confidence as the artificial-intelligence trade shows signs of strain,” The Wall Street Journal reported.
But analysts also warned that such circular financing among investors, suppliers, and customers has made it difficult to evaluate real market demand for AI-related hardware and services, according to the Journal.
TSMC’s chip fabrication plants physically produce the vast majority of Nvidia’s chips designed for AI data center workloads and make most of Apple’s custom chips used in iPhones, Mac laptops and desktops, plus Apple’s planned AI computing server. The rapid-fire announcement of awards tells us a few things about NASA’s efforts to return to the Moon and establish a durable settlement there during the next decade.

Schlafanalyse: Wie eine Open-Source-KI deinen Schlaf auf die Sekunde genau auswertet
Forschende der FH Aachen haben das KI-Modell AnySleep zur Schlafanalyse von Menschen entwickelt. Das Modell soll Schlafphasen besonders fein analysieren können, indem es schon kurze Veränderungen in der Gehirnaktivität erkennt. Die Forschungsergebnisse wurden kürzlich im Fachjournal npj Digital Medicine, das zum Nature Portfolio gehört, veröffentlicht. Künftig könnte das Werkzeug dabei helfen, Muster, die für bestimmte Krankheiten typisch sind, aufzuspüren.
KI-Modell zur Schlafanalyse
Bei Schlafanalysen wird die Gehirnaktivität meist per Elektroenzephalografie (EEG) aufgezeichnet. Für die Auswertung teilen Fachleute die Daten einer Nacht üblicherweise in 30-Sekunden-Abschnitte ein und ordnen jedem Abschnitt ein Schlafstadium zu. Das Ergebnis ist ein stufenförmiges Bild des Schlafverlaufs. SpaceX develops its own ‘Kessel’ rack-scale system featuring 72 Nvidia Rubin GPUs for data centers in space, report claims — replaces conventional NVLink cable assemblies with a massive 84-layer printed circuit board
For terrestrial and orbital deployments.
SpaceX/xAI is developing a custom version of Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale AI system that replaces conventional NVLink cable assemblies with a massive 84-layer printed circuit board (PCB), in part for use in orbital data centers, reports SemiAnalysis. The system is codenamed Kessel and retains 36 Vera CPUs, 72 Rubin GPUs, and nine NVLink switch trays, but introduces a different solid-state interconnect architecture. While SpaceX/xAI will continue to buy Nvidia hardware directly from the company, Elon Musk's company will source other components independently, which could give it greater control over its hardware supply chain.
The Kessel system retains the fundamental configuration of Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, which comprises 72 GPU packages distributed across 18 compute trays and nine NVLink switch trays. However, instead of Nvidia's conventional arrangement with internal NVLink cable cartridges, SpaceX plans to position compute and switch trays back-to-back around a passive PCB midplane. The architecture resembles a smaller version of Nvidia's Kyber design with 576 AI GPUs (albeit in 144 packages), which also relies on a PCB-based interconnect rather than conventional cable assemblies, SemiAnalysis notes. …

OpenClaw is creating a new privileged access problem for security teams
Though very useful, OpenClaw introduces major security challenges
OpenClaw’s meteoric rise is easy to understand. Unlike a chatbot that stops at answering a question, it is designed to take action across the tools people use every day: reading and sending email, managing calendars, working with documents, triggering workflows and, depending on configuration, interacting with financial tools or shell access. That is exactly what makes the technology useful, and exactly why security teams should pay close attention.
Advanced Services Lead at Arcova.
The core issue is not simply that OpenClaw uses AI. It is that a single assistant can aggregate access across systems that organizations have historically secured separately. Once one tool can read private data, communicate on a user’s behalf and trigger actions across multiple environments, it becomes a privileged control point. If an attacker can manipulate that point, the blast radius can extend far beyond the assistant itself.
From productivity tool to privileged operator
Tools like OpenClaw create an attractive path for attackers because they concentrate permissions across email, financial accounts, communication channels and local systems. Instead of targeting a rigid, deterministic workflow, an attacker may be targeting a system that interprets natural-language instructions and context before deciding what to do next. IBM Corp. today announced the Quantum Nighthawk r3, its next-generation processor designed to tackle larger, more complex computations at high speed while maintaining quality.
The company also said that in 2027, IBM plans to link two r3 quantum processors into a single system capable of running up to 10,000 quantum operations, scaling to more than 1,000 qubits between them.
“Useful quantum computing hinges on whether results can be delivered with accuracy and speed, both are fundamental,” said Director of IBM Research Jay Gambetta. “IBM Nighthawk is already showing us what that looks like today.”
The new r3 chip follows the introduction of Nighthawk r2 in September, which supports more than 7,500 quantum operations on 120 qubits.
Qubits are the fundamental unit of logical information in a quantum computer, similar to a classical computer’s bit. Unlike classical bits, which can be a 0 or 1, qubits can be 0, 1 or a “superposition” of both at the same time. Using this property, quantum processors such as IBM’s Nighthawk can do rapid, complex parallel calculations.
The r2 chip introduced a groundbreaking high-speed qubit reset architecture that lets developers and researchers quickly prime qubits after measurements. AMD's Madhu Rangarajan, corporate VP of Compute and Enterprise AI, says the company never set out to build its Zen 6 EPYC 9006 "Venice" chips around agentic AI, a not-so-subtle dig at NVIDIA and Arm, which both pitch their latest server CPUs as made for that exact job. Chief Zen architect Mike Clark said much the same in a separate talk, admitting AMD didn't see agentic computing coming, though he added that the company always expected the CPU to keep a role in AI software. We think that the EPYC 9006 CPU is the best CPU for the agentic era, and spoiler alert, we didn't magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing and purpose-built something for agentic. A medida foi anunciada nesta quarta-feira (11/11), um dia depois de o governo espanhol pedir a suspensão temporária da rede social.
Os conteúdos acumulavam pelo menos 48 milhões de visualizações, enquanto mais de 26 mil perfis participaram de interações com o material. O pedido foi apresentado ontem (10/11) pela ministra da Juventude e Infância, Sira Rego. O governo acionou o Ministério Público e a AEPD para avaliar medidas contra a rede social, segundo a NBC News.
A ministra defendeu a interrupção das atividades do TikTok até a remoção do material denunciado. Entretanto, nenhuma suspensão total foi determinada e a AEPD decidiu, até o momento, apenas pela suspensão dos conteúdos.
O levantamento foi conduzido pela organização espanhola Maldita.es, que analisou o TikTok durante 35 dias, entre setembro e outubro de 2026. Os pesquisadores identificaram 231 perfis responsáveis por 1.183 publicações com imagens e vídeos de abuso sexual infantil.

El hallazgo, realizado por Kaspersky, se hizo a principios de 2026 (aunque los detalles se conocieron recientemente) durante una campaña de ciberespionaje contra organizaciones diplomáticas de Asia Central y fue denominado como BlackX.
Qué es BlackX y por qué elude el Secure Boot
BlackX pertenece a la categoría de los bootkits: programas maliciosos que se ejecutan durante el proceso de arranque del equipo, antes de que el sistema operativo cargue por completo. Esa particularidad le permite interferir con los mecanismos de seguridad desde un punto anterior a cualquier defensa convencional.
Según la empresa, se trata de una versión modernizada de BlackLotus, un malware que se comercializaba en la dark web desde 2022. Su método de ataque aprovecha una vulnerabilidad conocida como Baton Drop, que permite sortear Secure Boot, la función de Windows diseñada para impedir que se ejecute software no confiable durante el inicio del equipo.
Lo que vuelve crítico este descubrimiento es que la falla sigue siendo explotable incluso en dispositivos que ya tienen instalado el parche de Microsoft. Trois mois après l’interdiction du démarchage sans votre accord, des sénateurs s’inquiètent de voir les appels continuer.
« Plusieurs mois après l’entrée en vigueur de la loi, les pratiques perdurent ! Certains concitoyens signalent encore près de cinq appels indésirables par jour », a dénoncé devant le Gouvernement le sénateur de la Haute-Saône Olivier Rietmann, rapporteur de la loi, le 20 octobre. articles.title: Agent sandboxing: Google's Agent Substrate isolates AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Agents may soon be the main workload, and most of the time they’re doing nothing
As AI agents take on more enterprise work, agent sandboxing has become a basic requirement rather than an afterthought. Every agent that writes code, runs tools or drives a browser needs hard walls around it. Those walls also can’t come at the cost of runaway compute bills.
Google LLC’s answer is Agent Substrate, an open-source project built on Kubernetes that the company donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation alongside its gVisor sandbox. Customers have raised the same problem for the past 18 months: They need to run agentic workloads securely and efficiently on the infrastructure they already have, according to Brandon Royal (pictured, left), product manager, AI agents and infrastructure, at Google Cloud.
“Any agent needs to be fully isolated,” Royal said. “Whether it’s accessing tools or using a computer or a browser, there needs to be some level of isolation, period, full stop.”
Royal and Benjamin Elder (right), staff software engineer at Google, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how agent sandboxing is central to Google’s open-source Agent Substrate. (* Disclosure below.)

articles.title: Cloud engineering teams must protect AI agent data in use - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
AI agents carry memory and storage like people, so their data needs guarding while in use
As AI agents move into production on Kubernetes, cloud engineering teams at financial companies face a security problem that encryption alone can’t solve. Container orchestration has become the default foundation for AI workloads, and the data those agents use is now the main target.
Payment networks feel that pressure more than most because every transaction carries customer data and regulatory exposure. Protecting data while it is being processed, and not just while it is stored or moving, has become central to running agents at scale, according to Krishna Mayuram (pictured), senior principal engineer and vice president of cloud engineering at Mastercard Inc.
“What we call confidential computing is when you are launching these applications in a highly secure, virtualized secure environments or confidential environments or confidential containers, you are able to protect the data in use,” Mayuram said. “We have protected data at rest, data in motion. Now, what is happening to the data in use?”
Mayuram spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed cloud engineering, security problems and the challenges of protecting data in use. (* Disclosure below.)

La fusée allemande Spectrum de la start-up Isar Aerospace accélère la cadence. Son troisième vol pourrait avoir lieu dès la fin du mois, un signal fort pour la souveraineté spatiale européenne.
En mars 2025, Spectrum réalisait son tout premier vol depuis Andøya, en Norvège. Si celui-ci s’est soldé par un échec, Isar Aerospace a vite souhaité remettre le pied à l’étrier. Après plusieurs reports, la société a retenté sa chance le 5 septembre dernier.
Et cette fois, tout s’était déroulé comme prévu : la fusée a atteint l’orbite et largué ses charges utiles. Une première pour une entreprise privée depuis l’Europe continentale, qu’elle compte réitérer très rapidement, révèle European Spaceflight.
Une fenêtre de tir approche
En effet, le troisième vol de Spectrum pourrait avoir lieu dès le 26 novembre. Un avis aérien publié le 28 octobre par Avinor, l’organisme norvégien de navigation aérienne, indique qu’une fenêtre de tir s’ouvre ce jour-là depuis Andøya, et reste valable jusqu’au 17 février 2027.
Ainsi, les tentatives seront possibles chaque soir entre 20h00 et 21h30. Si Isar Aerospace n’a pas encore communiqué de date précise, la fusée, elle, est en phase d’assemblage final, a fait savoir Daniel Metzler, son P.-D.G. Mais elle doit encore passer des tests avant de prendre la direction du pays nordique.

articles.title: The UK could be forced to spend £4 billion to replace outdated smart meters thanks to 2G and 3G switch-offs
articles.summary:
Millions of UK smart meters will need replacing thanks to the 3G and 2G switch-offs — and it won’t be cheap
A £4 billion upgrade
- Many UK smart meters rely on 2G and 3G connectivity
- With these networks being switched off, up to 13 million smart meters could soon need replacing
- This is estimated to cost around £4 billion
It hasn't been all that long since smart meters began rolling out (it took until October 2021 for the UK to have 15 million installed), but already, many of the early smart meter models could soon need replacing — because of something the government knew was going to happen.
Many current smart meters rely on 2G and 3G connections, but 3G has largely been phased out already, and there’s an official deadline of 2033 for 2G to follow suit — the UK's networks are actually planning to start this process in either 2029 or 2030.
This will leave roughly 12-13 million smart meters unable to transmit readings back to energy suppliers. In other words, they won’t be smart anymore, and will need replacing at a reported cost of around £4 billion (via The Register).
A predictable problem
None of this should come as a surprise to the UK government, which was behind the original push to roll out smart meters, given that it announced plans to phase out 2G and 3G back in 2021, after which some 2G and 3G smart meters continued to be installed.
But surprise or not, the process is set to be expensive, with the costs likely to be added to UK energy bills — which are already out…

Qué información hay que eliminar antes de usar un chatbot
Antes de compartir el archivo con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial, es necesario borrar el nombre completo, teléfono, correo, domicilio, enlaces privados, nombres de empleadores y copias de documentos.
Además, se debe omitir datos protegidos por acuerdos de confidencialidad, como resultados internos, listas de clientes, procesos de negocio o proyectos que aún no son públicos.

Enterprises, not a handful of giants, are becoming the GPU buyers that matter
Enterprises building AI-native applications are discovering that raw GPU capacity is only half the equation. As Kubernetes users move from cloud-native to AI-native stacks, the question is shifting from who has the most accelerators to who can run distributed, secure workloads at global scale.
The first wave of so-called neoclouds stood up massive GPU clusters for a handful of the largest buyers, but enterprise developers need far more than data center capacity. The Constant Company LLC, which does business as Vultr, has bet on AMD silicon and open software stacks to win AI infrastructure deals. It is positioning itself as a full-stack cloud built to close that gap, according to Kevin Cochrane (pictured), chief marketing officer of Vultr.
“In the early market … it was all about just standing up large GPU clusters wherever you could get land, power and shell, and then just selling it on through to a hyperscaler,” Cochrane said. “And somehow in that mix, people forgot that you still need cloud, right? You still gotta run this thing.”

A plataforma já entrou em modo somente leitura e deixará de funcionar em 20 de novembro.

“A Comunidade de Suporte da Apple será encerrada permanentemente em 20 de novembro de 2026. A partir de hoje, o site não aceitará mais novas postagens e está disponível em modo somente leitura”, diz o texto, que agradece aos usuários que “dedicaram o próprio tempo e conhecimento para ajudar outros”.
No comunicado, a empresa orienta os usuários que precisarem de ajuda com produtos a procurar informações nas páginas de Suporte. A empresa não informou o motivo exato para o fim do canal interativo.
O encerramento dá fim ao espaço que começou a funcionar em 1998, originalmente com o nome Apple Tech Exchange, para que usuários publicassem dúvidas e ajudassem outros proprietários da companhia. O fórum passou por diferentes reformulações ao longo dos anos, mas sempre manteve o mesmo foco.

Los modelos incluyen versiones con hasta 256 núcleos (las unidades internas que ejecutan instrucciones) y están orientados a tareas como inteligencia artificial, servicios en la nube, investigación científica y simulaciones técnicas.

To be at the frontier of quantum computing, industry-relevant applications demand both computational quality and speed. articles.summary:
Red Hat and Nvidia’s OpenShell puts AI agents on a deny-by-default leash
Prompt injection attacks and silent data exfiltration have turned AI agent security from a theoretical worry into an urgent enterprise concern.
As agents move from developer laptops into data centers, companies need guardrails that don’t strip away what makes agents useful. Red Hat Inc. and Nvidia Corp. have expanded their partnership to tackle that problem through OpenShell, an open-source project that sets limits on what agents can do. The threat model for agents differs sharply from that of traditional software, so the industry has to build a shared standard to secure them, according to Derek Carr (pictured, left), senior distinguished engineer at Red Hat.
“Agents can’t get access to your secrets. They need deny-by-default networking, and you need a rich policy framework for what happened and when for this class of apps,” Carr said. “Nvidia had reached out to us and noted that they were seeing the same problem domain. No one wants to work on this alone. It’s better to work together.”
Carr and Mrunal Patel (right), distinguished engineer at Red Hat, spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how OpenShell helps enterprises run AI agents in production with safeguards against prompt injection and data leaks. (* Disclosure below.)

articles.title: Víctimas de Grok demandan a xAI, la empresa de Musk, por convertir fotos de su infancia en imágenes sexuales
articles.summary:
Una joven identificada como Jane Doe 5 es una de las demandantes contra xAI, la empresa de inteligencia artificial de Elon Musk: un adulto usó el chatbot Grok para convertir una foto de su graduación escolar, tomada a los 14 años, en material de abuso sexual infantil, informó Bloomberg.
Según el reportaje de la agencia, la joven se enteró cuando un investigador policial le mostró la fotografía original y le hizo preguntas. El responsable fue el hermano mayor de una compañera que aparecía en la imagen. Manipuló la foto hasta crear una imagen sexual explícita de ella y la compartió en internet.
“Es imposible saber cuántos otros depredadores sexuales de menores poseen ahora el material de abuso de Jane Doe 5, ni hasta qué punto se difundió por canales de la red oscura”, dice la demanda que ella presentó, citada por Bloomberg.
El caso es uno de varios que se acumularon contra xAI desde marzo. Bloomberg describe un número creciente de víctimas que buscan que la compañía responda ante la justicia por imágenes que, según ellas, son casi imposibles de borrar de internet.
Las demandas se acumularon desde marzo
El 16 de marzo, tres jóvenes de Tennessee, dos de ellas menores de edad, demandaron a xAI en un tribunal federal de San José, California, según informó Reuters. Pidieron que el caso se tramite como demanda colectiva para quienes fueron identificables en imágenes sexualizadas creadas por Grok a partir de fotos reales.

Wednesday, November 11th 2026
Mounting Finished-Goods Inventories Prompt Some PC OEMs to Adjust Memory Procurement Plans for 2027
More than a year of rising memory prices has placed mounting cost pressure on the consumer electronics industry, according to TrendForce's latest memory industry research. Notebook shipments, in particular, are expected to decline sharply quarter-over-quarter beginning in 3Q26, leaving PC OEMs grappling with sluggish sales and swelling finished-goods inventories. 
Against this backdrop, some manufacturers are planning to adjust memory procurement for 4Q26—and even 1Q27—while considering a greater reliance on private-label models in their shipment mix.TrendForce notes that PC OEMs brought forward some of their procurement and production schedules to the first half of 2026 in anticipation of further memory price increases. However, higher retail prices have dampened sales across Asia and Europe, while finished-goods inventories have been gradually rising among OEMs and in North American distribution channels.
Notebook shipments fell 15.8% QoQ in 3Q26, with a further single-digit percentage decline possible in 4Q26. These mounting inventory pressures are prompting some OEMs to reassess their product strategies for 2027, including plans to expand the share of private-label models while incorporating lower-specification memory chips and CPUs with fewer cores.

articles.title: Robots de Google hacen más de 200 tareas: desde servir comida hasta manipular objetos de laboratorio
articles.summary:
Google DeepMind presentó Gemini Robotics 2.5, un modelo de inteligencia artificial que permite a los robots aprender más de 200 tareas nuevas en semanas en lugar de meses y ejecutarlas en fábricas reales con un 96% de éxito.
El sistema combina visión, lenguaje y acción, lo que en la práctica significa que el robot ve un objeto, entiende qué se le pide y mueve brazos y manos para lograrlo, sin que un programador le indique cada movimiento paso a paso.
Qué tareas pueden hacer estos robots
Gemini Robotics 2.5 fue evaluado en más de 200 tareas distintas, desde servir comida con pinzas hasta atar un lazo en una caja de regalo o manipular líquidos con una pipeta.
Gemini Robotics 2.5 es el modelo de Google DeepMind que combina visión, lenguaje y acción para que un robot interprete una orden, reconozca un objeto y lo manipule de forma autónoma, con mejoras de hasta el cien por ciento en la tasa de éxito frente a su versión anterior. Esa capacidad lo acerca a actividades que antes requerían la destreza manual de una persona.
Según las pruebas de la compañía, el modelo logra entre un 30% y un 100% más de éxito que la versión previa, dependiendo del tipo de tarea, y completa esas tareas entre un 20% y un 30% más rápido.
El modelo funciona en distintos cuerpos robóticos. Uno de ellos es el humanoide Apollo 2, de la empresa Apptronik, que incorpora una mano de cinco dedos con 22 grados de libertad llamada SharpaWave. También opera en la plataforma Franka Duo, equipada con pinzas de dos de…

articles.title: Google's former CEO thinks AI has a marketing problem — but what if Americans understand the technology perfectly well and just don't like what it's doing?
articles.summary:
‘Our industry does a terrible job of marketing our benefits': Google's former CEO Eric Schmidt thinks AI has a PR problem — but maybe people understand it just fine
Ex-Google boss believes AI companies just need to up their marketing
Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt thinks AI struggles to convince Americans that it's a net good because of its messaging. After the U.S. election exposed growing public hostility toward AI, particularly the data centers necessary to power the technology, Schmidt argued in an Axios interview that the companies have done a poor job explaining the benefits of their products, but he is underestimating how much people already understand about AI.
"Our industry does a terrible job of marketing our benefits," Schmidt said. "We talk about all the negatives without talking the positives, and people are much more likely to index their minds on the negatives."
Millions have experienced ChatGPT and Google's Gemini firsthand for good and ill. They're perfectly capable of appreciating those benefits while remaining unhappy about the industry's growing influence over their lives.
Product or pitch?
AI data centers became increasingly contentious during the November midterms, with voters frustrated by electricity costs and the environmental consequences of large computing facilities. articles.title: Un robot construit seul une structure dans l’espace pour la toute première fois : le champ des possibles s’ouvre
articles.summary:
Pour la première fois, un robot a assemblé seul une structure en orbite. Une démonstration qui pourrait changer la façon dont on construira les futurs engins spatiaux.
Le secteur spatial est en pleine ébullition. Entre les méga-constellations de satellites, les projets de data centers en orbite et la conquête de la Lune, c’est une toute nouvelle économie qui est en train de naître. Mais cette croissance se frottera forcément à une limite : la capacité d’emport des lanceurs, qui est obligatoirement limitée. Et si ASTRA changeait la donne ?
Une petite antenne d’1,4 mètre
C’est le nom d’un petit robot conçu par des chercheurs de la prestigieuse université Caltech et financé par la DARPA, l’agence de recherche du Pentagone. Il s’inscrit dans le cadre du programme NOM4D, dont l’objectif est de construire de très grandes structures dans l’espace.
Lancé le 30 mars dernier à bord d’une fusée Falcon 9 de SpaceX, il est niché dans un véhicule orbital de la société Momentus, et tient dans un volume d’environ 1 mètre cube. Cela paraît très restreint, certes, mais assez pour renfermer la machinerie et les matériaux nécessaires à la construction. Sa mission : construire une antenne d’1,4 mètre de large.
Ainsi, son bras articulé a attrapé des tubes en fibre composite et des joints en aluminium dans ses réserves, puis les a assemblés comme un jeu de Meccano pour former l’ossature de l’antenne qui compte pour l’instant trois modules. Deux d’entre eux ont été préassemblés : ASTRA s’est chargé …

articles.title: 10 funciones de la IA de Amazon para encontrar las mejores promociones durante las compras navideñas
articles.summary:
La temporada navideña reúne miles de productos, descuentos temporales y cambios de precio que pueden dificultar la comparación antes de comprar. La inteligencia artificial (IA) de Amazon incorpora funciones para rastrear promociones, recibir avisos y organizar las compras desde la aplicación y el sitio web.
Estas herramientas permiten establecer precios objetivo, consultar la evolución de un artículo, detectar reposiciones y pedir sugerencias según listas o búsquedas previas. Algunas funciones pueden variar según el país, el producto y la versión de la aplicación, así que hay que revisar si están habilitadas en cada cuenta.
Cómo recibir alertas cuando un artículo baje de precio
Alexa para compras puede avisar cuando aparezcan promociones en categorías concretas o cuando un producto alcance un importe definido. Es posible pedir alertas para auriculares con cancelación de ruido o ingresar en la ficha de un artículo y solicitar una notificación cuando su valor baje.
De qué forma activar una compra automática con un precio límite
Quienes ya decidieron qué producto quieren comprar pueden fijar un valor máximo y autorizar la compra automática. La orden se completa con el método de pago predeterminado si el artículo baja hasta el importe establecido.
Antes de habilitar esta opción, resulta conveniente revisar la dirección de entrega, las condiciones de devolución y el presupuesto disponible para evitar compras que ya no sean necesarias.

The attacker could also have seen requests being processed on that server that day, including requests sent in confidential mode, the company said earlier this week. That mode processes requests inside a trusted execution environment (TEE) designed to keep them private even from the company itself.
But the TEE "does not protect against a vulnerability in the software running inside the environment," the company said. SGLang runs inside the TEE, which is how the attacker could reach requests there.
That access has since been closed, but not before the attacker moved further into the company's systems.
The attacker reached an internal system behind Private Chat, a product the company had already deprecated. So far, the company has confirmed that the attacker downloaded account details for about 100 users there. These are email addresses and names, and for some accounts, plan and balance information.
The company found no sign that stored Private Chat conversations or uploaded files were accessed.
The attacker also reached 18 AI agents on an older deployment of NEAR AI Agents that did not run inside the company's TEE. From those agents, the attacker took data including chat history, settings and logs.

articles.title: Git Patches Flaw That Lets Malicious Repositories Execute Code During Recursive Clones
articles.summary:
A flaw in Git can let a malicious repository run an attacker's code on a computer that clones it recursively, together with its submodules. The Git project fixed it this week in Git 2.56.1, with matching fixes for the 2.50 through 2.55 series in 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1 and 2.55.1.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-111760, is an integer truncation in how Git handles its index. An extremely long path in a repository can pass Git's safety check, but Git then writes it to disk under a shorter name that an attacker can set to .git.
This lets an attacker replace a submodule's .git file with a symbolic link to a folder holding malicious hooks or configuration. Hooks are programs Git runs at set points, so once Git uses that folder, the attacker's code can run.
Submodules matter here because Git refuses to replace a .git folder with a symbolic link, but in a freshly cloned submodule, .git is a file.
The fixed versions, listed in the Git project's release announcement, refuse such extremely long paths before their length can be cut short.
GitHub, which ships Git in its own tools, explained the fixes in a detailed write-up. It advises installing a fixed version from your operating system or Git distributor, and updating any app that ships its own copy of Git.
The company has already applied the fixes to github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For GitHub Enterprise Server, they are in versions 3.19.15, 3.20.11, 3.21.9 and 3.22.4.

articles.title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
articles.summary:
An AI model can be given a hidden backdoor by editing fewer than 10 of its rarely used neurons, without retraining the model, Microsoft researchers have shown.
When a chosen trigger appears, the model outputs an attacker's command, which an agent using that model would run with the agent's own permissions. The attacker must be able to change the model's weights.
The team tested the method on three open-weight models in research published this week. Microsoft says it has not seen any threat actors use the technique. The company also published guidance on defending against it.
The edited neurons are ones that rarely fire and barely affect the model's answers. They were set to fire only when a trigger string appears, either in a user's request or later in a tool's output.
The researchers call the method Lazarus. Each edited neuron forces one token of the command into the model's output, so a command needs about one neuron per token.
The new neuron settings are calculated directly and can then be tuned with a few hundred training steps on those neurons alone. Nothing else in the model file or the code that runs it changes.
In a researcher's walkthrough posted on X, a backdoored Nemotron-Terminal-8B model with 10 edited neurons was tasked with fixing a Node.js server. It worked normally for three turns.

AI provider keys that customers stored on Railway were stolen in an October breach and used to commit an estimated $740,000 in unauthorized spending, the platform-as-a-service provider said yesterday. It has promised to pay those charges itself when an AI provider will not refund them.
The company builds and runs apps for its customers and stores their secrets, such as API keys and database credentials, as environment variables. The attacker decrypted variables in at most 1.85% of workspaces, about 100,000, and its database queries looked for AI provider keys.
In an October 26 update, the company told customers asking about refunds for unauthorized AI spend that "Railway is unable to refund customers for spend performed with compromised API keys." It encouraged them to contact the AI providers directly and offered to escalate their requests.
According to the company's incident report, the decrypted data also included linked-account tokens for 1,852 users: BYOK agent keys and GitHub OAuth tokens. All were reset, each user was notified, and no logins to customer accounts using stolen credentials were found.
In addition to AI keys, one of the attacker's database queries matched cloud, database, and payment service credentials. The company's forensics did not show any customer databases being accessed, and there was no indication that customers' code repositories were downloaded.

articles.title: eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise
articles.summary:
The in-house Python script behind eMudhra's October key compromise has now cost the company 8 more of its intermediate certificate authorities (CAs), even though it did not weaken their keys.
Each intermediate CA has its own private key, which the company uses to sign the certificates it issues. The 8 intermediate CAs compromised in October had a different problem: a single line in the script cut each of their keys to one byte, the company said this week.
The script also retrieved the RSA keys of the 8 newly revoked CAs from the company's hardware security modules (HSMs). The company says it cannot show that the keys were handled as required by its own rules. It revoked the CAs late last week.
The company had called those CAs unaffected. "The RSA issuers went through a different path as per our assessment of the code and are therefore not impacted," it wrote on Mozilla's bug tracker on October 19.
Of the 8, 6 were for website (TLS) certificates and 2 for code signing. The company had put 4 of them into production in May. Its list names 195 certificates from them, 29 for its own domains.
Both problems began at a key ceremony on April 30, 2025, according to the full incident report the company posted to the same bug tracker this week. That day it generated 16 CA keys on Utimaco HSMs, including the 8 behind the October key compromise.

articles.title: Así son las alfombras eléctricas para calentar el hogar y ahorrar energía
articles.summary:
Las alfombras eléctricas calefactadas son una alternativa económica al suelo radiante para calentar la casa sin necesidad de obras. Su funcionamiento se basa en resistencias internas que generan calor por radiación, con un consumo que puede bajar la factura de luz si se combinan de forma correcta con la calefacción tradicional.
A diferencia de las mantas eléctricas pensadas para el regazo, estos dispositivos se instalan en el suelo y soportan el peso de quien camina sobre ellas e incluso de muebles livianos como mesas bajas.
Qué son y cómo funcionan las alfombras térmicas
Una alfombra térmica es un emisor de calor eléctrico que mantiene una temperatura de consigna para evitar que el frío se acumule en las zonas bajas de una habitación.
En su interior combinan capas antideslizantes e impermeables con un sistema de cables calefactores ubicados entre dos materiales aislantes. La corriente eléctrica que circula por esos cables calienta el aislante, que a su vez transmite el calor al suelo.
El calor se emite por radiación y se distribuye hacia arriba por convección. Las alfombras trabajan a temperaturas máximas de entre 30 °C y 40 °C, por lo que no queman al tacto, y suelen incorporar varios niveles de regulación para ajustar la intensidad según la necesidad del momento.
La mayoría incluye un mando de control similar al de las mantas eléctricas, con el que se elige la potencia o la temperatura deseada. También pueden conectarse a un enchufe inteligente para manejarlas a distancia …

At its core is KytyPS5, the same PS5 emulator that recently got Marvel's Wolverine to run on PC, and showed good progress in many other PS exclusive titles. Rather than emulating the PS5's processor, KytyPS5 hands the game's x86-64 code straight to the host CPU. Hammedi's patch gets around it by translating those instructions into older SSE4.2, AVX, and BMI1 equivalents, mostly at load time. articles.title: We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned.
articles.summary:
We tell customers three things about securing AI agents: they need their own identities, access that fits the job they’re given, and traceability that’s separate from any human’s. That was true for us at Token as well. Then, we built an agent that broke all three by default.
This helped us think through how such agents should be defended. When a browser agent acts inside a user’s authenticated session, the application may see the user but not the agent, the delegation, or the task’s intended scope. By creating an agent that breaks all the security rules, Token learned how companies should be using identity to gain control, especially as agent use scales. Standards are coming, but there are steps security teams can take today.
The agent we would have flagged
The agent we created is named Rehearsal. Its job is to answer questions inside the Token platform by doing rather than telling. It autonomously opens pages in the browser tab, sets filters, and fills in forms.
From a security perspective, it’s a typical UI agent that runs in the user’s browser. That’s what makes it useful. But it also means the agent runs within the user’s session and has their reach.
Moreover, to the server behind the page, the agent’s clicks are inherently indistinguishable from the user’s, because nothing in a session cookie points to who the session driver is.

Zoom has released software updates to address two security flaws impacting Zoom Workplace for Windows, including a critical bug that could result in privilege escalation on affected systems.
The vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-108186 (CVSS score: 9.6) - An improper input validation vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user to conduct an escalation of privilege via network access.
- CVE-2026-108187 (CVSS score: 8.1) - An origin validation vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user to conduct an escalation of privilege via network access.
Successful exploitation of either of the shortcomings could permit remote attackers to escalate privileges without requiring any special permissions or access.
While CVE-2026-108187 affects Zoom Workplace for Windows before version 7.1.5, CVE-2026-108186 impacts versions starting from 7.1.0 and before 7.1.8.
Earlier this July, the popular videoconferencing platform shipped fixes for another improper input validation flaw impacting Zoom Workplace for Windows (CVE-2026-53412, CVSS score: 9.8) that could enable an unauthenticated user to take control of accounts.
Although Zoom makes no mention of the vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, users are advised to apply the latest patches to mitigate potential threats.

El Banco Central de Paraguay intervino el 3 de noviembre el banco digital Ueno y suspendió de inmediato su aplicación, sus tarjetas y todos sus servicios. Unos 2,9 millones de clientes, cerca del 60% de los adultos del país, quedaron sin acceso a su dinero, según la propia entidad y el medio NPR.
La decisión del directorio del Banco Central fue unánime y se tomó después de que el índice de solvencia de Ueno cayera por debajo de la mitad del mínimo exigido, según informó BBC Mundo.
El Banco Central activó un proceso de resolución: todos los activos y pasivos de la entidad quedaron congelados hasta determinar cómo se cubren sus obligaciones. La directiva del organismo Liana Caballero confirmó en una conferencia de prensa que ningún servicio de Ueno seguía activo.
Quién recibió su dinero y quién sigue esperando
El Banco Central informó que Ueno tenía alrededor de 1,8 millones de depositantes. Los ahorros se devuelven con el Fondo de Garantía de Depósitos, que cubre hasta 75 salarios mínimos por persona, unos 228,3 millones de guaraníes (cerca de USD 38.000).
La devolución comenzó con quienes tenían hasta 10 millones de guaraníes (unos USD 1.600), sin deudas con Ueno y con una cuenta en otro banco. Hasta el 9 de noviembre, más de 1,7 millones de personas habían recuperado todo o parte de su dinero y se habían devuelto unos USD 341 millones, según el Banco Central.

El sistema, pensado para futuros robots domésticos y de asistencia, fue presentado en la conferencia anual Conference on Robot Learning, según MIT News.
En las pruebas virtuales —simulaciones desarrolladas por el equipo para validar el sistema—, un brazo robótico llevó a cabo tres tareas: servir café, trasladar una vela y transportar una bola de bowling. En todos los casos, el robot siguió la instrucción literal y extendió su razonamiento a objetos no mencionados: evitó otros dispositivos electrónicos, materiales inflamables y objetos frágiles.

articles.title: 'Model weights need the same level of scrutiny as code': Microsoft researchers find AI agents can be backdoored by editing just a few neurons
articles.summary:
'Model weights need the same level of scrutiny as code': Microsoft researchers find AI agents can be backdoored by editing just a few neurons
What if your AI agent behaved normally and then just "snapped"?
- Researchers demonstrated a “sleeper agent” AI attack by modifying a handful of dormant neurons inside an LLM
- The backdoor remains hidden until a specific trigger appears, then executes attacker-defined actions
- Defenders are urged to verify model integrity, audit weights, and tightly restrict AI agent permissions
It sounds like an idea for a sequel to The Manchurian Candidate: a seemingly ordinary AI agent has been secretly programmed to turn evil, carrying out his master’s nefarious task only when a specific trigger activates his conditioning.
Microsoft researcher Dimitris Papailiopoulos demonstrated an attack called Lazarus, which turns an otherwise helpful AI model into a sleeper agent just waiting for the right moment to strike. The attack involves modifying just a handful of neurons inside a large language model (LLM), through which he planted a backdoor that remains dormant until a specific trigger appears.
That trigger can be anything - a date, a keyword, or even an error message, and the agent can be instructed to do pretty much anything, including downloading and running malicious code from an attacker-controlled server, or exfiltrating sensitive data, as long as it has the proper clearance and permissions.

articles.title: IA : non, le bain de sang dans l'emploi n'aura pas lieu, selon Yann Le Cun
articles.summary:
On craint beaucoup que l'intelligence artificielle ne mette tout le monde rapidement au chômage. Une crainte totalement infondée pour Yann Le Cun.
C'est la crainte majeure - hormis l'apocalypse d'une IA superintelligente qui nous voudrait du mal. La technologie de l'intelligence artificielle pourrait détruire un nombre immense d'emploi, jusqu'à, pour de nombreux économistes, en détruire encore plus que la révolution industrielle. Pourtant loin des paroles cataclysmique d'un Dario Amodei, Yann Le Cun ne croit pas du tout à l'effondrement du marché du travail.
« Seule une faible proportion des tâches est aujourd’hui automatisable »
S'il existe une figure de l'intelligence artificielle qui a tendance à modérer l'enthousiasme ou la peur créés par l'intelligence artificielle générative, c'est bien le chercheur français Yann Le Cun. Et il vient de le faire à nouveau dans une interview donnée au journal Le Point.
Dans celle-ci, il rejette toutes les prédictions apocalyptiques sur le marché du travail. Il explique qu'à son sens, nous sommes non seulement encore très loin des IA plus intelligentes que les êtres humains, mais aussi que la technologie ne va pas détruire les emplois. Pour lui, on devrait plutôt voir naître des métiers inédits. Par ailleurs, de manière plus global, « seule une faible proportion des tâches est aujourd’hui automatisable. »

SpaceX is seeking regulatory approval to build a natural-gas power facility for its planned $24 billion artificial-intelligence computing complex in Texas.
The application covers 35 natural gas turbines with a combined electricity generation capacity of 748 megawatts (MW).
The project will be located in Starbase, where SpaceX operates its rocket launch facilities, and includes plans for the company to develop and operate both facilities.
SpaceX plans dedicated power generation for its Texas computing facility
The proposed development would allow SpaceX to generate electricity independently rather than rely entirely on connections to Texas's main power grid.

articles.title: I wore the Google Fitbit Edge for a week, and even though its GPS is a little ropey, its wellness and fitness tracking smarts won me over
articles.summary:
TechRadar Verdict
The Google Fitbit Edge is a simple band-based tracker that harkens back to Fitbits of yore — notably the Charge and Luxe series. While I dislike the Google Health app, which has difficulty surfacing historic numbers on its free tier, and is overly reliant on its chatbot for its premium tier, the band is comfortable and unobtrusive. Its tactile button offers just the right amount of interaction to be useful, and not enough to be distracting. GPS and resulting metrics are a little wobbly, but for most people looking for an activity tracker for sports, the gym, and the occasional jog or bike ride, the Edge will do the trick.

- + Affordable
- + Clean, simple UI
- + 7-day battery life
- + Accurate fitness, health and automatic activity tracking
Reasons to avoid
- - GPS and pace aren’t 1-1 accurate compared with top trackers
- - Messy Google Health app orientated around premium chatbot service
